source.title: Isolation of cuspidal spectrum, with application to the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture
source.authors: Raphaël Beuzart-Plessis, Yifeng Liu, Wei Zhang and Xinwen Zhu
readSections: arXiv 1912.07169v3 (19 June 2021, 'minor revision; 48 pages; to appear in Annals of Mathematics'), read in full from its TeX source, the file GGP_Annals_fin.tex (e-print SHA-256 6dd3c272ef2f716ceac30991cf0472db4d6bcb26c8c4e1858a4d9193dc4cd5cc; fetched from arxiv.org on 2026-09-23), with the PDF (SHA-256 f2834146d4fee02b38c4849ee9a7ef76a3dbc1131e7eef799e6f95b0f0d0ac13) for numbering and pages: §1 Introduction (Theorems 1.1–1.10), §2 Multipliers of the Schwartz convolution algebra, §3 Isolation of spectrum, §4 Application to the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture, Appendix A (Delorme's theorem for reductive groups) and the bibliography.

The Annals version (pp. 519–584, September 2021) is paywalled and was not read. v3 is the authors' final version: posted three months before publication as a minor revision 'to appear in Annals', its source file is named for the Annals, and it thanks the referee. Numbers and pages below are those of the arXiv PDF.

Cited inputs (Zydor, Chaudouard–Zydor, W. Zhang, Xue, Yun, Beuzart-Plessis, Delorme, Donnelly, Kostant, Flicker, Ramakrishnan, Sakellaridis) were not read; items that rest on one state it as the paper uses it.

summary: The paper isolates prescribed cuspidal pieces of the automorphic L²-spectrum by multipliers of the convolution algebra of Schwartz test functions, and uses this to prove the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for U(n) × U(n+1) in the stable case (Theorem 1.8), a nonvanishing theorem for central Rankin–Selberg values (Theorem 1.9) and the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for tempered stable pairs (Theorem 1.10), removing the earlier requirement of a split place where both representations are supercuspidal. §2 constructs multipliers μ⋆ of the Schwartz algebra S(G) of a real reductive group for every W-invariant holomorphic μ of moderate growth along the sets Y*_ϑ attached to the real form (Theorem 2.13), extending Delorme (Appendix A) by difference operators and Kostant's tensor-product theory; §3 combines these with spherical Hecke operators and Donnelly's bound on cuspidal eigenvalues to annihilate every cuspidal component of the coarse Langlands decomposition except those in which a given character occurs (Theorems 3.6, 3.7, 3.19); §4 runs Zydor's Jacquet–Rallis relative trace formulas with multipliers compatible under base change, which preserve smooth transfer (Proposition 4.8), and also proves weak base change for unitary groups without the endoscopic classification (Theorem 4.14). The atlas plans the (g, K)-module foundations (AF.1), finiteness of automorphic forms (AF.2), the spectral decomposition (AS.4), Rankin–Selberg integrals (AL.3), the Mok/KMSW classification (ML.4) and the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent (ML.5); the Gan–Gross–Prasad framework is pending in GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups. Nothing plans Schwartz multipliers, Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula, the isolation theorems, or the Jacquet–Rallis global trace formulas and their comparison beyond the local layers pending in JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison (PAPER-ZHANG-21). Reviewed by REV-PAPER-BEUZARTPLESSIS-LIU-ZHANG-ETAL-21 (Claude Code, cc-2aeb03) and corrected in place: 128 items (0 library, 7 planned, 121 missing). 47 mistakes are confirmed (33 misprints, 7 gaps, 7 errors; 2 reach a stated result, 8 a proof). Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4 (= 2.13) stand, the other gaps being repairable. Theorems 1.8–1.10 and 4.14 rest on extending Chaudouard–Zydor's equality of geometric sides to archimedean test functions in the completed Schwartz space, which the paper asserts by density without argument (E39); the extension is expected to hold. Theorem 4.14(4) needs π cuspidal automorphic (E45). Not formalised.

items.name: Theorem 1.1: isolating the nearly isotypic cuspidal part of a non-CAP representation
items.statement: Let F be a number field, G a connected reductive group over F, Z the maximal F-split torus in the centre of G, and K ⊂ G(A_F^∞) an open compact subgroup. Let π = ⊗_v π_v be an irreducible admissible representation of G(A_F) with unitary automorphic central character ω (L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) is formed with ω restricted to Z(A_F), as in §3.1). Suppose that there is no pair (P, σ), P a proper parabolic subgroup of G (defined over F) and σ a cuspidal automorphic representation of M(A_F), M the Levi quotient of P (σ not required to be unitary: twists σ ⊗ ξ_s, s ∈ a*_{M,C}, count), such that π_v is a constituent of Ind_P^G(σ_v) for all but finitely many places v of F. Then there is a multiplier μ⋆ of the algebra S(G(A_F))_K such that for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K: (1) R(μ⋆f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)_π, the π-nearly isotypic subspace of L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω), i.e. the direct sum of the K-invariants of the irreducible subrepresentations π̃ (of L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω)) with π̃_v ≅ π_v for all but finitely many places v of F; (2) π(μ⋆f) = π(f).
items.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.1, p. 2; special case of Theorem 3.6 (T = S, χ = χ_{π^T})
items.note: Remark 1.2: it fails for compactly supported test functions; the Schwartz algebra is essential.

items.name: Theorem 1.3: isolating one cuspidal component for Res_{F′/F} GL_n
items.statement: Let F be a number field, F′/F a finite extension, G = Res_{F′/F} GL_n (so Z ≅ G_m is its maximal F-split central torus), K ⊂ G(A_F^∞) open compact, and π an irreducible admissible representation of G(A_F) with unitary automorphic central character ω. The non-CAP hypothesis of Theorem 1.1 is not assumed. Suppose that π is an irreducible constituent of Ind_P^G(σ) for a parabolic subgroup P of G and a cuspidal automorphic representation σ (not necessarily unitary) of the Levi quotient M of P. Then there is a multiplier μ⋆ of the algebra S(G(A_F))_K such that for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K: (1) R(μ⋆f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω), the cuspidal component of L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) associated to (M, σ) (i.e. to the cuspidal datum of σ, taken up to twist by a*_{M,C} and conjugacy); (2) π(μ⋆f) = π(f).
items.locator: §1.1, Theorem 1.3, pp. 2–3; deduced after Theorem 3.19, p. 29, from Theorem 3.19 (T = S, χ = χ_{π^T}) and strong multiplicity one for Res_{F′/F} GL_n ([PS79]; the classification [JS81, Theorem 4.4] is cited before the theorem, p. 2)

items.name: Definition 1.5: conjugate self-dual and hermitian representations of GL_n(A_E)
items.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F of number fields with involution c and an isobaric automorphic representation Π of GL_n(A_E): Π is conjugate self-dual if Π^∨ ≅ Π ∘ c; Π is hermitian if it is an isobaric sum of mutually non-isomorphic cuspidal Π_1, …, Π_d, each conjugate self-dual with L(s, Π_i, As^{(−1)^n}) regular at s = 1.
items.note: Equivalently each Π_i has the conjugate-self-dual sign (−1)^{n−1} of U(n)-parameters; for cuspidal Π exactly one Asai L-function has a pole at s = 1.

items.name: Definition 1.6: weak automorphic base change
items.statement: For a hermitian space V over E of rank n, G = U(V) and an irreducible admissible π of G(A_F), an isobaric automorphic Π of GL_n(A_E) is a weak automorphic base change of π if for almost all places v of F split in E, the split local base change of π_v is isomorphic to Π_v. It is unique up to isomorphism (Ramakrishnan, Theorem A) and denoted BC(π).
items.note: Weaker than the usual notion (no local–global compatibility at nonsplit places), chosen to keep the argument independent of the endoscopic classification of unitary groups.

items.name: Theorem 1.8: the global Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for U(n) × U(n+1), stable case
items.statement: Let Π_n, Π_{n+1} be hermitian cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n(A_E), GL_{n+1}(A_E). The following are equivalent: (1) L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0; (2) there are a hermitian space V_n of rank n (with V_{n+1} = V_n ⊕ E·e, e of norm 1), for m = n, n+1 irreducible subrepresentations π_m ⊆ A_cusp(G_m), G_m = U(V_m), with BC(π_m) ≅ Π_m, and cusp forms φ_m ∈ π_m with 𝒫(φ_n, φ_{n+1}) = ∫_{G_n(F)∖G_n(A_F)} φ_n(h)φ_{n+1}(h) dh ≠ 0 (Tamagawa measure).
items.note: Previously known when Π_n and Π_{n+1} are supercuspidal at a prime of E split over F (Zhang, Xue, Beuzart-Plessis). Remark 4.17 strengthens (1) ⇒ (2) with archimedean compatibility and hyperspecial fixed vectors.

items.name: Theorem 1.9: a nonvanishing theorem for central Rankin–Selberg values
items.statement: For every hermitian cuspidal automorphic Π_{n+1} of GL_{n+1}(A_E) there is a hermitian cuspidal automorphic Π_n of GL_n(A_E) with L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0.

items.name: Theorem 1.10: the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for U(n) × U(n+1), stable tempered case
items.statement: In the situation of (2) of Theorem 1.8, if π_n and π_{n+1} are everywhere tempered, the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture (R. N. Harris's formulation, Conjecture 1.2) holds for π_n and π_{n+1}.
items.note: The proof uses the endoscopic classification of generic packets (Mok, Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White) and the local Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture, and then follows Beuzart-Plessis's proof of his Theorem 5 in 'Plancherel formula for GL_n(F)∖GL_n(E)…'.

items.name: The Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for unitary groups (Harris's formulation)
items.statement: (Ichino–Ikeda; formulated for U(n) × U(n+1) in R. N. Harris, IMRN 2014, Conjecture 1.2; see also W. Zhang, JAMS 27 (2014), Conjecture 1.1.) Let G = U(V_n) × U(V_{n+1}) with H = U(V_n) embedded diagonally, and let π = π_n ⊠ π_{n+1} be a cuspidal automorphic representation of G(A_F) with π_v tempered for every v. Give H(A_F) the Tamagawa measure dh = ∏_v dh_v. Fix a factorisation ⟨·,·⟩_Pet = ∏_v ⟨·,·⟩_v of the Petersson inner product. Put L(s, π) = Δ_{n+1} L(s, BC(π_n) × BC(π_{n+1})) / L(s + ½, π, Ad), where Δ_{n+1} = ∏_{i=1}^{n+1} L(i, η_{E/F}^i) and L(s, π, Ad) = L(s, π_n, Ad) L(s, π_{n+1}, Ad), and let L(s, π_v) be its local factor. Put α_v^♮(φ_v, φ_v) = L(½, π_v)^{-1} ∫_{H(F_v)} ⟨π_v(h)φ_v, φ_v⟩_v dh_v. Then for every decomposable φ = ⊗_v φ_v ∈ π, |𝒫(φ)|² / ⟨φ, φ⟩_Pet = |S_π|^{-1} · L(½, π) · ∏_v α_v^♮(φ_v, φ_v) / ⟨φ_v, φ_v⟩_v. Here 𝒫(φ_n ⊗ φ_{n+1}) = ∫_{H(F)∖H(A_F)} φ_n(h) φ_{n+1}(h) dh, and S_π is the (finite elementary abelian 2-) component group of the L-parameter of π. The paper cites the conjecture and does not restate it.
items.note: The GGP candidate's brief reserves the refined (Ichino–Ikeda) conjecture for the first consumer that needs it; this paper is that consumer.

items.name: The local Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture for unitary groups (Beuzart-Plessis)
items.statement: (Beuzart-Plessis, Astérisque 418 (2020), the archimedean case, which is the reference [BP20] the paper cites; at places split in E the statement is elementary) Let v be an archimedean place of F or a place split in E. For a tempered L-parameter of U(n) × U(n+1) over F_v, exactly one member of its Vogan packet (the union over V_v ∈ 𝔙_v of the L-packets of G^{V_v}(F_v)) is H^{V_v}(F_v)-distinguished. Consequently, for a finite set □ of such places, the local Jacquet–Langlands map Temp_{H^V_□}(G^V_□) → Temp(G^{qs}_□)/stab (from H^V_□-distinguished tempered representations to stable tempered classes of the quasi-split group) is injective.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Lemma 4.9, p. 36; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.10, p. 43
items.note: GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups lists this known case ('unitary p-adic and real tempered, Beuzart-Plessis') among its cited theorems.

items.name: Schwartz functions and the Schwartz algebra of a real reductive group
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over R and G = G(R). A Schwartz function on G is a smooth function f such that Df is bounded for every algebraic differential operator D ∈ 𝒟(G) ([Wal83, §§2.5–2.6]). Footnote 1: this is not Harish-Chandra's Schwartz space, which is defined by a much weaker condition. S(G) is the algebra of Schwartz functions under convolution (f_1 ∗ f_2)(g) = ∫_G f_1(gh^{-1}) f_2(h) dh. It carries a natural Fréchet topology in which convolution is continuous. For every admissible representation of G, or more generally every Fréchet representation of moderate growth (π, V_π), π(f)v = ∫_G f(g) π(g) v dg converges absolutely for f ∈ S(G) and v ∈ V_π, and defines a continuous operator π(f). In §1.1 the same definition is applied on G(F_∞), and S(G(A_F))_K denotes the bi-K-invariant Schwartz test functions on G(A_F): Schwartz at the archimedean places, compactly supported smooth at the finite places.
items.note: Not Mathlib's SchwartzMap (on normed spaces): here the growth is measured by algebraic differential operators on the group.

items.name: Multipliers of an algebra
items.statement: For a complex algebra 𝒮, Mul(𝒮) is the algebra of linear maps μ⋆ : 𝒮 → 𝒮 with μ⋆(f ∗ g) = (μ⋆f) ∗ g = f ∗ (μ⋆g) for all f, g ∈ 𝒮.

items.name: Definition 2.1: subsets of C of rank p
items.statement: Let Λ ⊆ C and let p ≥ 0 be an integer. Λ has rank p if (1) Λ is countable, and (2) p is the least nonnegative integer such that Σ_{λ∈Λ, λ≠0} |λ|^{−(p+1)} converges. (Λ is said to be of finite rank if it has rank p for some p; the phrase is used in Corollary 2.5 and in §3.3, p. 26.)
items.note: Classical complex analysis; the pinned Mathlib has no Weierstrass factorisation.

items.name: Definition 2.3: holomorphic functions of moderate vertical growth
items.statement: Let U be a finite-dimensional real vector space. A holomorphic function μ on U_C has moderate vertical growth if for every M > 0 there is r_M ∈ R such that sup_{z∈U_C, ‖Re z‖<M} |μ(z)|·(1 + ‖z‖)^{r_M} < ∞; this holds for one Euclidean norm ‖·‖ on U_C if and only if it holds for every one. (Printed with |ν(z)| in place of |μ(z)|: sourceIssues E2.)
items.note: Printed with ν for μ in Definition 2.3 (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Definition 2.8: the spaces M_θ(h*_C), N_θ(h*_C) and M^♯_θ(h*_C)
items.statement: Fix a root datum (X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨) with Weyl group W. Let Aut(X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨)^♡ be the set of its automorphisms of order at most 2 (stable under conjugation by W); h* := X* ⊗_Z R; for ϑ ∈ Aut^♡ let h*_ϑ (resp. h*^−_ϑ) be the +1- (resp. −1-) eigenspace of ϑ on h*, and Y*_ϑ the projection of ρ + X* ⊆ h* onto h*^−_ϑ (along h*_ϑ), where ρ is the half-sum of the positive roots for any base of Φ (Y*_ϑ does not depend on the base and is a translate of a discrete subgroup of h*^−_ϑ; for a subgroup H of h*_{ϑ,C}, H ⊕ Y*_ϑ denotes {α + ϖ : α ∈ H, ϖ ∈ Y*_ϑ}). Let θ ⊆ Aut^♡ be stable under W-conjugation. (1) M_θ(h*_C) is the space of holomorphic functions μ on h*_C such that for every ϑ ∈ θ and every M > 0 there is r_{ϑ,M} ∈ R with sup_{α∈h*_{ϑ,C}, ‖Re α‖<M, ϖ∈Y*_ϑ} |μ(α+ϖ)|·(1 + ‖α+ϖ‖)^{r_{ϑ,M}} < ∞ (2.1), for some, equivalently every, Euclidean norm ‖·‖ on h*_C. (2) N_θ(h*_C) is the space of holomorphic μ on h*_C such that the same supremum with exponent r is finite for every ϑ ∈ θ, every M > 0 and every r ∈ R. (3) M^♯_θ(h*_C) is the subspace of M_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C) of those μ such that for every ϑ ∈ θ, μ restricted to h*_{ϑ,C} + ϖ is zero for all but finitely many ϖ ∈ Y*_ϑ. When θ = {1} the subscript is suppressed (since h*_1 = h* and Y*_1 = {0}, M(h*_C) is the space of holomorphic functions of moderate vertical growth).

items.name: Lemma 2.10: nonvanishing elements of M^♯_θ
items.statement: For every α_0 ∈ h*_C there is μ ∈ M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W with μ(α_0) ≠ 0.
items.note: From Corollary 2.6 applied, for each ϑ, to a lattice of h*^−_{ϑ,C} containing Y*_ϑ. Correction: θ must be finite; the set of all involutions of the root datum can be infinite (E16).

items.name: The Harish-Chandra isomorphism, infinitesimal characters and Casselman–Wallach representations
items.statement: Z(g) ≅ C[h*_C]^W (Harish-Chandra), so characters of Z(g) are W-orbits in h*_C and μ(χ) makes sense for μ ∈ O(h*_C)^W; admissible representations are smooth admissible Fréchet representations of moderate growth (Casselman–Wallach), equivalent to Harish-Chandra (g, K)-modules by taking K-finite vectors; each irreducible one has an infinitesimal character χ_π.
items.note: AF.1 plans (g, K)-modules, the centre of U(g) with infinitesimal-character subspaces, and the Casselman–Wallach globalisation.

items.name: Theorem 2.13 (= Theorem 1.4): multipliers of the Schwartz algebra of a real reductive group
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over R, G = G(R), (X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨) the root datum of G_C (weight and coweight lattices of its abstract Cartan group, roots and coroots), W its Weyl group, h* = X* ⊗ R, and θ the W-stable set of elements of Aut(X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨)^♡ of the form wϑ with w ∈ W and ϑ ∈ Aut^♡ inducing the real form G of G_C. For every μ ∈ M_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W there is a unique linear operator μ⋆ : S(G) → S(G) such that π(μ⋆f) = μ(χ_π)·π(f) for every f ∈ S(G) and every irreducible admissible representation π of G. In particular, μ⋆ ∈ Mul(S(G)) is a multiplier of S(G).
items.note: Proof: first for N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W with L²-bounds (Proposition 2.24), then μ_n = exp(−P(α/n))μ with a positive W_θ-invariant homogeneous polynomial P.

items.name: Remark 2.14: the refined invariant θ_G of a real reductive group
items.statement: (G connected reductive over R, θ as in §2.3.) The set θ determines only the inner class of G. Let θ_G ⊆ Aut(X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨)^♡ be the set of elements obtained, as in Lemma 2.19, from all maximal tori T of G (and all universal isomorphisms T_C ≅ H). It is contained in θ and stable under W-conjugation, and: θ_G = θ if and only if G is quasi-split; 1 ∈ θ_G if and only if G is split; −1 ∈ θ_G if and only if G has an anisotropic maximal torus; θ_G = {−1} if and only if G is anisotropic.

items.name: Lemma 2.18: elements of M^♯_θ see only finitely many K-types
items.statement: For μ ∈ M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W there is a finite set 𝔗(μ) of K-types such that every irreducible admissible π with μ(χ_π) ≠ 0 contains a member of 𝔗(μ).
items.note: Proof: Harish-Chandra's discrete series infinitesimal characters leave finitely many (M, σ) up to conjugation and unramified twist; Langlands quotients inherit the minimal K-types of their standard modules (Knapp, Thm. 15.10). Correction: the proof must include limits of discrete series (E21).

items.name: Harish-Chandra's discrete series infinitesimal characters, the Langlands classification and minimal K-types (inputs to Lemma 2.18)
items.statement: As used in the proof of Lemma 2.18: (a) (Harish-Chandra [HC66]) the infinitesimal characters of the discrete series σ of the Levi subgroups M of G are given by their Harish-Chandra parameters. Consequently, for a Levi M with fundamental maximal torus T and ϑ ∈ θ_G ⊆ θ attached to T (Lemma 2.19), the infinitesimal characters of the parabolic inductions of σ ⊗ ξ (ξ unramified) lie in h*_{ϑ,C} ⊕ Y*_ϑ, the Y*_ϑ-component being fixed by σ. For each ϖ ∈ Y*_ϑ only finitely many pairs (M, σ), up to conjugation and unramified twist, give infinitesimal characters in h*_{ϑ,C} + ϖ (up to W). (b) (Langlands classification) every irreducible admissible representation of G is the Langlands quotient of a standard module. (c) ([Kna01, Theorem 15.10]) the Langlands quotient of a standard module contains the minimal K-types of that standard module.

items.name: Lemma 2.19: maximal tori give elements of θ
items.statement: For a maximal torus T of G with T = A_T T_c and a universal isomorphism T_C ≅ H inducing h* = a*_T ⊕ i t*_c, there is a unique ϑ ∈ θ with a*_T = h*_ϑ and i t*_c = h*^−_ϑ (ϑ is induced by complex conjugation on T).

items.name: Lemma 2.20: elements of 𝒮 preserving polynomials act continuously on O(h*_C), with seminorm bounds
items.statement: (G, θ as in §2.3; ℛ ⊆ 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒯 and p_{ϑ,M,r} as in §2.4.) Let S ∈ 𝒮 satisfy S(C[h*_C]) ⊆ C[h*_C]. Then S extends uniquely to an endomorphism of O(h*_C) that is continuous for the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets (still denoted S). Moreover there exist M_S > 0 and r_S > 0 such that for every M > 0 and every r ∈ R there is C_{S,M,r} > 0 with p_{1,M,r}(Sμ) ≤ C_{S,M,r}·p_{1,M+M_S,r+r_S}(μ) and max_{ϑ∈θ} p_{ϑ,M,r}(Sμ) ≤ C_{S,M,r}·max_{ϑ∈θ} p_{ϑ,M+M_S,r+r_S}(μ) for every μ ∈ O(h*_C). In particular: (1) S preserves N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C); (2) if S(C[h*_C]) ⊆ C[h*_C]^W, then S preserves N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W.
items.note: Lemma 2.21's proof has |u| = 1 where |u| ≤ 1 is needed (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Kostant: the centraliser R_τ is a finitely generated free Z(g)-module
items.statement: (Kostant, J. Funct. Anal. 20 (1975), Theorem 4.8) Let (τ, W_τ) be a finite-dimensional algebraic representation of G and δ : U(g) → U(g) ⊗ End(W_τ) the algebra homomorphism with δ(X) = X ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ τ(X) for X ∈ g. Then the centraliser R_τ of δ(U(g)) in U(g) ⊗ End(W_τ) is a finitely generated free Z(g)-module, where Z(g) acts on U(g) ⊗ End(W_τ) by z.(u ⊗ A) = (zu) ⊗ A.

items.name: Lemma 2.22: the action of the centre on R_τ by difference operators
items.statement: Let (τ, W_τ) be a finite-dimensional algebraic representation of G, δ : U(g) → U(g) ⊗ End(W_τ) the homomorphism X ↦ X ⊗ 1 + 1 ⊗ τ(X), and R_τ the centraliser of δ(U(g)), a finite free Z(g)-module for z.(u ⊗ A) = (zu) ⊗ A (Kostant); identify Z(g) with C[h*_C]^W by the Harish-Chandra isomorphism. Then for every basis v_1, …, v_r of R_τ over Z(g) there exist S_1, …, S_r ∈ 𝒮 with S_i C[h*_C] ⊆ C[h*_C]^W such that δ(z) = Σ_{i=1}^r S_i(z) v_i for every z ∈ Z(g).

items.name: Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula
items.statement: (Harish-Chandra, Ann. of Math. 104 (1976)) There is a Borel measure dπ on the tempered dual Temp(G) of G such that ‖f‖²_{L²(G)} = ∫_{Temp(G)} ‖π(f)‖²_{HS} dπ for every f ∈ S(G), where ‖·‖_{HS} is the Hilbert–Schmidt norm.

items.name: Proposition 2.24: Theorem 2.13 for rapidly decreasing μ, with L²-bounds
items.statement: Theorem 2.13 holds for μ ∈ N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W. Moreover, for every algebraic differential operator D there is M_D > 0 such that for every f ∈ S(G) and r there is C_{D,f,r} with ‖D(μ⋆f)‖_{L²} ≤ C_{D,f,r}·max_{ϑ∈θ} p_{ϑ,M_D,r}(μ) for all such μ.
items.note: Proof: Delorme's multipliers on bi-K-finite functions (Proposition A.1), the Plancherel formula for D = 1, and for polynomial D the identity P(μ⋆f) = Σ S_i(μ) ⋆ P_{ij} L(u_{ij}) f from Lemma 2.22, checked on generic principal series (Lemma 2.25).

items.name: Lemma 2.25: generic principal series tensored with τ are semisimple
items.statement: Let (τ, W_τ) be a finite-dimensional algebraic representation of G, P_0 = M_0N_0 a minimal parabolic subgroup of G, σ an irreducible (finite-dimensional) representation of M_0, and σ_ξ = σ ⊗ ξ for ξ an unramified character of M_0. Then for ξ in general position the admissible representation I_{P_0}^G(σ_ξ) ⊗ τ (normalised parabolic induction) is semisimple, that is, a direct sum of irreducible admissible representations.

items.name: L²-spectrum with central character, quasi-cuspidal test functions
items.statement: Let F be a number field, G a connected reductive group over F, Z the maximal F-split torus in the centre of G, dg = ∏_v dg_v the fixed Haar measure on G(A_F), and ω: Z(A_F) → C^× a unitary automorphic character. L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) is the L²-completion of the space of smooth functions φ on G(A_F) with φ(zγg) = ω(z)φ(g) for all z ∈ Z(A_F), γ ∈ G(F), g ∈ G(A_F), and with |φ|² integrable on Z(A_F)G(F)∖G(A_F). G(A_F) acts on it by the right regular representation R, which preserves the subspace L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) of cuspidal functions, and the algebra S(G(A_F)) = S(G_∞) ⊗ S(G(A_F^∞)) (Definition 3.1) acts continuously on it via R. Definition 3.2: a Schwartz test function f ∈ S(G(A_F)) is ω-quasi-cuspidal (quasi-cuspidal when ω = 1) if the image of the endomorphism R(f) of L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) is contained in L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω).
items.note: AF.3 and AS.4 plan cusp forms and the L²-spectrum; the Schwartz test functions acting on it and quasi-cuspidality are new.

items.name: Definition 3.3: T-characters (with the spherical Hecke algebras H_G^T)
items.statement: Let S_G be the set of primes v of F at which G_v is ramified; K_0 = ∏_v K_{0,v} is a fixed maximal compact subgroup of G(A_F), with K_{0,v} hyperspecial of volume 1 for v ∉ S_G. For a prime v ∉ S_G, H_{G,v} := C[K_{0,v}∖G(F_v)/K_{0,v}] is the spherical Hecke algebra (unit 1_{K_{0,v}}); for a (possibly infinite) set T of primes containing S_G, H_G^T is the restricted tensor product of the H_{G,v}, v ∉ T. Definition 3.3: a T-character (for G) is a pair χ = (χ_∞, χ^{∞,T}) with χ_∞ a character of Z(g) (g the complex Lie algebra of G ⊗_Q C) and χ^{∞,T} a character of H_G^T. For v ∉ T the v-component χ_v, a character of H_{G,v}, gives rise to a K_{0,v}-spherical irreducible admissible representation of G(F_v), unique up to isomorphism; an irreducible admissible π = ⊗_v π_v of G(A_F) with π_v^{K_{0,v}} ≠ {0} for every prime v ∉ T has the induced T-character χ_{π^T} = (χ_{π_∞}, χ_{π^{∞,T}}).
items.locator: §3.1, Definition 3.3 and the surrounding paragraphs, p. 22

items.name: Theorem 3.6: isolation for non-CAP characters
items.statement: Standing data (§3.1, p. 22): a unitary automorphic character ω of Z(A_F); a set T of primes of F containing S_G and a T-character χ = (χ_∞, χ^{∞,T}); a finite set S of primes with S_G ⊆ S ⊆ T; a subgroup K ⊆ K_0^∞ of finite index of the form K = K_S × ∏_{v∉S} K_{0,v}. Theorem 3.6: suppose that χ is not (G, T)-CAP (Definition 3.4). Then there exists a T-multiplier μ of S(G(A_F))_K (Definition 3.5) such that for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K, (1) R(μ⋆f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)[χ]; (2) μ(χ) = 1. In particular, μ⋆f is an ω-quasi-cuspidal Schwartz test function (Definition 3.2).

items.name: Theorem 3.7: isolation inside the cuspidal spectrum
items.statement: Standing data (§3.1, p. 22): a unitary automorphic character ω of Z(A_F); a set T of primes of F containing S_G and a T-character χ = (χ_∞, χ^{∞,T}); a finite set S of primes with S_G ⊆ S ⊆ T; a subgroup K ⊆ K_0^∞ of finite index of the form K = K_S × ∏_{v∉S} K_{0,v}. Theorem 3.7: there exists a T-multiplier μ of S(G(A_F))_K such that for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K, (1) R(μ⋆f) maps L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)[χ]; (2) μ(χ) = 1. (No CAP hypothesis on χ.)

items.name: The coarse Langlands decomposition by cuspidal data
items.statement: (Langlands [Lan76, Lemma 4.6(i)]; Mœglin–Waldspurger [MW95, II.2.4]) With 𝔇(G, ω)^♡ as in Definition 3.9: L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) = ⊕̂_{(M,σ)∈𝔇(G,ω)^♡} L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) (3.1), a Hilbert direct sum (the coarse Langlands decomposition; (M, σ) ∈ 𝔇(G, ω)^♡ is a cuspidal datum and L²_{(M,σ)} its cuspidal component). The component is constructed as follows: for (M, σ) ∈ 𝔇(G, ω), 𝒜^G_{(M,σ)} is the space of R(K_0)-finite smooth φ on N_{P_M}(A_F)∖G(A_F) such that for every x ∈ K_0 the function m ↦ δ_{P_M}^{−1/2}(m)φ(mx) is an automorphic form on M(A_F) lying in L²(M, σ); for a Paley–Wiener function Φ: a*_{M,C} → 𝒜^G_{(M,σ)} with values in a finite-dimensional subspace, Φ̃(g) := ∫_{i a*_M} Φ_s(g) ξ_s(m(g)) ds for g ∈ P_M(F)∖G(A_F), where m(g) is the image in Z(A_F)M(A_F)^1∖M(A_F) of the M(A_F)-component of g in the Iwasawa decomposition G(A_F) = N_{P_M}(A_F)M(A_F)K_0; the pseudo-Eisenstein series E(g, Φ) := Σ_{γ∈P_M(F)∖G(F)} Φ̃(γg) lies in L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω), and L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) is the closure of the span of the E(−, Φ). L²_{(M,σ)} = L²_{(M′,σ′)} if and only if (M, σ) ≈ (M′, σ′). Taking R(K)-invariants gives (3.2): L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) = ⊕̂_{(M,σ)∈𝔇(G,ω)^♡} L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω), where L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) is the subspace of R(K)-invariants.
items.locator: §3.2, (3.1), the construction of cuspidal components and (3.2), p. 24
items.note: AS.4 plans the complete spectral decomposition over associate cuspidal data with Eisenstein wave packets; AS.1 the induced families.

items.name: Finiteness of cusp forms with fixed infinitesimal character, K-types and level
items.statement: (Harish-Chandra, LNM 62) There are only finitely many cuspidal automorphic representations of G(A_F), up to isomorphism, with a given infinitesimal character, a given finite set of K_∞-types and nonzero invariants under a given open compact subgroup.
items.note: AF.2 plans the finiteness of automorphic forms with fixed level, finitely many K-types and an infinitesimal-character ideal; AF.3 the finite multiplicity of cuspidal constituents.

items.name: Donnelly: counting cuspidal eigenvalues
items.statement: (Donnelly, 'On the cuspidal spectrum for finite volume symmetric spaces', J. Differential Geom. 17 (1982), Theorem 9.1: Weyl's upper bound for the cuspidal spectrum.) As used in the proofs of Lemmas 3.12–3.13: for a standard Levi subgroup M of G, the open compact subgroup K_{M_der} := K_M ∩ M_der(A_F^∞) and the finite set 𝔗_{M_der} of K^{M_der}_{0,∞}-types, let 𝔆(M_der; K_{M_der}, 𝔗_{M_der}) be the set of isomorphism classes of cuspidal automorphic representations ς of M_der(A_F) with ς^{K_{M_der}} ≠ {0} and ς|_{K^{M_der}_{0,∞}} containing a member of 𝔗_{M_der}. Then (i) the set of Casimir eigenvalues of the elements of 𝔆(M_der; K_{M_der}, 𝔗_{M_der}) is of finite rank (Definition 2.1); (ii) for every finite set A ⊆ C only finitely many elements of 𝔆(M_der; K_{M_der}, 𝔗_{M_der}) have Casimir eigenvalue in A.
items.note: Remark 3.20 mentions Müller's trace class theorem as the alternative for the Langlands decomposition by discrete data.

items.name: Definition 3.11: χ_∞-typical cuspidal data
items.statement: Let M be a standard Levi subgroup of G, M_der its derived subgroup, X*_M the weight lattice of (T ∩ M_der ⊗_Q R)_C (T the fixed maximal torus of G ⊗_Q R in M_0 ⊗_Q R) and b*_M := X*_M ⊗_Z R. The restriction X* → X*_M induces a surjection h* → b*_M; its kernel c*_M canonically contains a*_M. With the canonical decomposition h* = c*_M ⊕ b*_M, γ_M^+: h* → c*_M/a*_M and γ_M^−: h* → b*_M are the components of the quotient map γ_M: h* → h*/a*_M. The Weyl group W_M of (M ⊗_Q C, T_C) is a subgroup of W acting trivially on c*_M; for σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω) and s ∈ a*_{M,C}, the infinitesimal character χ_{σ_{s,∞}} is a W_M-orbit in h*_C whose image under γ_M does not depend on s, and χ^G_{σ_{s,∞}} denotes the infinitesimal character of Ind^G_{P_M}(σ_{s,∞}), i.e. the W-orbit of χ_{σ_{s,∞}}. The Casimir operator of M_der ⊗_Q R defines a W_M-invariant polynomial function λ_M: b*_{M,C} → C. Definition 3.11: σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω)^♡ is χ_∞-typical if γ_M^+(χ_{σ_∞}) ∈ γ_M^+(χ_∞) and λ_M(γ_M^−(χ_{σ_∞})) ∈ λ_M(γ_M^−(χ_∞)); 𝔆(M, ω)^♡_{χ_∞} denotes the set of χ_∞-typical elements of 𝔆(M, ω)^♡.
items.locator: §3.3, Definition 3.11 and the preceding paragraphs, p. 25

items.name: Lemma 3.12: the Casimir values of 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M) form a set of finite rank
items.statement: For every standard Levi subgroup M of G, with K_M, 𝔗_M and 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M) as constructed in §3.3 (see the missing construction item), the subset Λ(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M) := {λ_M(γ_M^−(χ_{σ_∞})) | σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M)} ⊆ C is of finite rank (Definition 2.1).

items.name: Definition 3.16: a T-character occurring in a cuspidal datum
items.statement: For (M, σ) ∈ 𝔇(G, ω), the T-character χ occurs in (M, σ) if there exists s ∈ a*_{M,C} such that (i) χ^G_{σ_s,∞} = χ_∞ and (ii) for every prime v of F not in T, the spherical representation corresponding to χ_v is a constituent of Ind^G_{P_M}(σ_{s,v}). This property depends only on the class of (M, σ) in 𝔇(G, ω)^♡; 𝔇(G, ω)^♡_χ denotes the subset of 𝔇(G, ω)^♡ of classes in which χ occurs.
items.note: Printed with '(3.9)' for the decomposition (3.2) in Theorem 3.19 (sourceIssues E5).

items.name: Remark 3.20: the refinement by the Langlands decomposition
items.statement: (Remark 3.20) Using the Langlands decomposition L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) = ⊕̂_{(M,σ)∈𝔇′(G,ω)^♡} L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω)′ ([Lan76], as formulated in [Art05, Theorem 7.2]), which refines (3.1), where 𝔇′(G, ω) is the set of pairs (M, σ) with σ a discrete automorphic representation of M(A_F) with central character in Ω_M(ω) (with the analogous relation ≈), instead of (3.1), and Müller's trace class theorem [Mül89, Theorem 0.1] instead of [Don82, Theorem 9.1] in the proof of Lemma 3.12, Theorem 3.19 strengthens to: there is a T-multiplier μ of S(G(A_F))_K with μ(χ) = 1 such that for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K, R(μ⋆f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into ⊕̂_{(M,σ)∈𝔇′(G,ω)^♡_χ} L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)′, with 𝔇′(G, ω)^♡_χ defined as in Definition 3.16. This space is contained in ⊕̂_{(M,σ)∈𝔇(G,ω)^♡_χ} L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω), possibly strictly: for G = PGL_2, M the diagonal Levi subgroup and σ trivial, L²_{(M,σ)}(…/K, 1) = L²_{(M,σ)}(…/K, 1)′ ⊕ L²_{(G,σ̃)}(…/K, 1)′ with σ̃ the trivial character of G(A_F), and there are χ with (M, σ) ∈ 𝔇′(G, ω)^♡_χ (hence ∈ 𝔇(G, ω)^♡_χ) but (G, σ̃) ∉ 𝔇′(G, ω)^♡_χ, whereas (G, σ̃) ∈ 𝔇′(G, ω)^♡_χ always forces (M, σ) ∈ 𝔇′(G, ω)^♡_χ.

items.name: Delorme's multipliers for semisimple groups
items.statement: (Delorme, Duke Math. J. 53 (1986), Théorème 1.7) Let G be a real semisimple Lie group that is linear and connected (in the analytic topology), with maximal compact subgroup K. For every μ ∈ N(h*_C)^W, i.e. every W-invariant holomorphic function on h*_C with rapid decay on vertical strips, there is a linear operator μ⋆ : C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} → S(G)_{(K)} with π(μ⋆f) = μ(χ_π)·π(f) for every f ∈ C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} and every irreducible admissible representation π of G. As used in the proof of Proposition A.1, it is applied with support in a fixed compact set and K-types in a fixed finite set.
items.locator: Appendix A, after Proposition A.1 and in its proof, pp. 43–45; §1.3, p. 5 ('Essentially by a result of Delorme (Proposition A.1)')

items.name: Proposition A.1: Delorme's theorem for reductive groups
items.statement: For G = G(R) connected reductive and every μ ∈ N(h*_C)^W there is a unique linear μ⋆ : C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} → S(G)_{(K)} with π(μ⋆f) = μ(χ_π)·π(f) for every f and every irreducible admissible π.
items.locator: Appendix A, Proposition A.1 and proof, pp. 43–45
items.note: Printed with N(h*_C) for N(h*_C)^W (sourceIssues E8). Reduction to G^0 = (Z^0 × G^0_der)/Z^0_der, with Delorme for G^0_der and Sakellaridis for Z^0, then projective tensor products for fixed K-types and supports.

items.name: Lemma A.2: N(z*_C) ⊗̂ N(h*_{der,C})^W ≅ N(h*_C)^W
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over R with centre Z and derived group G_der, and let z* and h*_der be the real vector spaces spanned by the weight lattices of Z_C and of the abstract Cartan group of G_{der,C}, so that (A.4) induces h* = z* ⊕ h*_der (W acting trivially on z*). Let N(z*_C) and N(h*_{der,C}) be defined like N(h*_C) (holomorphic functions with rapid decay on vertical strips, with their Fréchet topologies). Then (μ_1, μ_2) ↦ μ_1 ⊗ μ_2 induces an isomorphism of Fréchet spaces N(z*_C) ⊗̂ N(h*_{der,C})^W ≅ N(h*_C)^W, ⊗̂ the completed projective tensor product. (Proof: the Paley–Wiener isomorphisms S(Z^0_sp) ≅ N(z*_C), S(H^0_der) ≅ N(h*_{der,C}), S(H^0) ≅ N(h*_C) for the split real tori with cotangent spaces z*, h*_der, h*, then S(Z^0_sp) ⊗̂ S(H^0_der) ≅ S(H^0) by [AG10, Cor. 2.6.3], then W-invariants.)
items.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.2 and proof, p. 44

items.name: The Jacquet–Rallis setup: groups, subgroups and regular semisimple orbits
items.statement: Let E/F be a quadratic extension of number fields with quadratic character η_{E/F} of A_F^×/F^×, and n ≥ 1. Put G′_n = Res_{E/F}GL_{n,E}, G′_{n+1} = Res_{E/F}GL_{n+1,E}, G′ = G′_n × G′_{n+1}; H′_1 ⊆ G′ is the graph of the embedding G′_n → G′_{n+1} via the first n coordinates and H′_2 = GL_{n,F} × GL_{n+1,F}. An element γ of G′ is regular semisimple if H′_1γH′_2 is Zariski closed in G′ and the natural map H′_1 × H′_2 → H′_1γH′_2 is an isomorphism; G′_rs ⊆ G′ is the Zariski open subset of such elements, B′ = H′_1∖G′/H′_2 (an affine variety over F) and B′_rs ⊆ B′ the image of G′_rs. Z′ is the maximal F-split centre of G′ (also the centre of H′_2), and η : H′_2(A_F) = GL_n(A_F) × GL_{n+1}(A_F) → C^× is the character (η_{E/F}^{n−1}∘det) ⊠ (η_{E/F}^n∘det), trivial on Z′(A_F)H′_2(F). 𝔙 is the set of isomorphism classes of pairs V = (V_n, V_{n+1}) of nondegenerate hermitian spaces over E with V_n of rank n and V_{n+1} = V_n ⊕ E·e, e of norm 1; for each place v there are a local analogue 𝔙_v and the localisation map 𝔙 → 𝔙_v, V ↦ V_v. For V ∈ 𝔙: G^V_n = U(V_n), G^V_{n+1} = U(V_{n+1}), G^V = G^V_n × G^V_{n+1}, H^V ⊆ G^V the graph of the natural embedding G^V_n → G^V_{n+1}; δ^V ∈ G^V is regular semisimple if H^Vδ^VH^V is Zariski closed in G^V and H^V × H^V → H^Vδ^VH^V is an isomorphism; G^V_rs, B^V = H^V∖G^V/H^V (affine over F) and B^V_rs (the image of G^V_rs) as before. B′ and B^V are canonically isomorphic (W. Zhang, Ann. of Math. 180 (2014), §3.1); for an F-algebra R, γ ∈ G′_rs(R) and δ^V ∈ G^V_rs(R) are a matching pair if their images in B′(R) = B^V(R) coincide.
items.note: After Jacquet–Rallis and W. Zhang (Ann. Math. 2014, §3.1).

items.name: Global relative characters and relative orbital integrals
items.statement: For Π ∈ 𝔆(G′,1) (cuspidal automorphic representations of G′(A_F) with trivial central character on Z′(A_F); Definition 3.9) there is a distribution I_Π on S(G′(A_F)) (Beuzart-Plessis, arXiv:1602.06538, §3.1) with I_Π(f′) = Σ_{φ∈B(Π)} (∫_{H′_1(F)∖H′_1(A_F)} (Π(f′)φ)(h_1) dh_1) · conj(∫_{Z′(A_F)H′_2(F)∖H′_2(A_F)} φ(h_2)η(h_2) dh_2) (4.1), B(Π) an orthonormal basis of Π for the Petersson inner product over G′/Z′ and dh_1, dh_2 the Tamagawa measures on H′_1(A_F), Z′(A_F)∖H′_2(A_F). For π^V ∈ 𝔆(G^V,1), J_{π^V}(f^V) = Σ_{φ∈B(π^V)} (∫_{H^V(F)∖H^V(A_F)} (π^V(f^V)φ)(h) dh) · conj(∫_{H^V(F)∖H^V(A_F)} φ(h) dh) (4.3) (Petersson inner product over G^V, dh Tamagawa). For every γ ∈ B′(F) (resp. δ^V ∈ B^V(F)) Zydor's distribution I_γ on S(G′(A_F)) (J. reine angew. Math. 762 (2020), Théorème 5.9) (resp. J_{δ^V} on S(G^V(A_F)), Théorème 6.6), stated there for C_c^∞ functions and asserted to extend to Schwartz functions (footnote 8), is a regularisation of relative orbital integrals; for γ ∈ B′_rs(F), I_γ(f′) = O_η(γ̃, f′) := ∫_{H′_1(A_F)×H′_2(A_F)} f′(h_1^{−1}γ̃h_2)η(h_2) dh_1 dh_2 for an arbitrary lift γ̃ ∈ G′_rs(F) of γ (4.2); for δ^V ∈ B^V_rs(F), J_{δ^V}(f^V) = O(δ̃^V, f^V) := ∫_{H^V(A_F)×H^V(A_F)} f^V(h_1^{−1}δ̃^V h_2) dh_1 dh_2 for an arbitrary lift δ̃^V ∈ G^V_rs(F) (4.4), and J_{δ^V}(f^V) := 0 when δ^V has no lift (G^V_rs(F) → B^V_rs(F) is not surjective; footnote 9).

items.name: Proposition 4.1: Zydor's Jacquet–Rallis relative trace formula for G′ and quasi-cuspidal Schwartz functions
items.statement: (Zydor, J. reine angew. Math. 762 (2020), Théorème 5.10; the paper asserts that its proof works for Schwartz test functions) Let f′ ∈ S(G′(A_F)) be a quasi-cuspidal Schwartz test function (Definition 3.2, ω = 1 on Z′(A_F)). Then Σ_{Π∈𝔆(G′,1)} I_Π(f′) = Σ_{γ∈B′(F)} I_γ(f′), both sums being absolutely convergent.
items.note: The paper asserts that Zydor's proofs for C_c^∞ work for Schwartz functions. The text after (4.4) says I_γ for J_{δ^V} (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Definition 4.3: relative hyperspecial maximal subgroups
items.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean place of F unramified in E. A subgroup K′_v of G′(F_v) is a relative hyperspecial maximal subgroup if K′_v = GL_n(O_{E_v}) × GL_{n+1}(O_{E_v}); a subgroup K^V_v of G^V(F_v) is a relative hyperspecial maximal subgroup if it is of the form U(L_n) × U(L_{n+1}) with L_n a self-dual lattice of V_{n,v} and L_{n+1} = L_n ⊕ O_{E_v}·e.

items.name: The Jacquet–Rallis relative fundamental lemma
items.statement: (Yun, Duke Math. J. 156 (2011), with an appendix by J. Gordon, for p large; Beuzart-Plessis, arXiv:1901.02653, in general) Let v be a nonarchimedean place of F unramified in E and K′_v = GL_n(O_{E_v}) × GL_{n+1}(O_{E_v}). Let V_v ∈ 𝔙_v. If V_{n,v} has a self-dual lattice L_n, then 1_{K′_v} and 1_{K^{V_v}_v}, K^{V_v}_v = U(L_n) × U(L_n ⊕ O_{E_v}e), have matching orbital integrals; otherwise 1_{K′_v} matches 0 on V_v, i.e. O_η(γ, 1_{K′_v}) = 0 for every γ ∈ G′_rs(F_v) matching an element of G^{V_v}_rs(F_v). Consequently Definition 4.4(2) is insensitive to the choice of □ (Remark 4.5), and tuples that are unit functions outside a finite set of places and match on it are complete smooth transfer, with f^V = 0 allowed for V ramified outside that set (pp. 38, 41).
items.locator: §4.2, Remark 4.5, p. 33; §4.3, proof of Proposition 4.13, p. 38; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.8, p. 41

items.name: Proposition 4.6: existence of smooth transfer
items.statement: (W. Zhang, Thm. 2.6 (nonarchimedean); H. Xue, Thm. 2.7 (archimedean)) At every place v there are dense subspaces S_tr(G′(F_v)) ⊆ S(G′(F_v)) and S_tr(G^{V_v}(F_v)) ⊆ S(G^{V_v}(F_v)), equal to the whole spaces if v is nonarchimedean or split in E, whose elements have smooth transfers: every f′_v ∈ S_tr has matching (f_v^{V_v})_{V_v}, and every f_v^{V_v} ∈ S_tr has a matching f′_v with f^{W_v}_v = 0 for W_v ≠ V_v.

items.name: Proposition 4.7 (Chaudouard–Zydor): equality of the geometric sides
items.statement: (Chaudouard–Zydor, Compos. Math. 157 (2021), Théorème 16.2.4.1, extended from pure tensors) If f′ and (f^V)_V are complete smooth transfer, then Σ_{γ∈B′(F)} I_γ(f′) = Σ_{V∈𝔙} Σ_{δ^V∈B^V(F)} J_{δ^V}(f^V), the sum over V being finite.
items.note: Correction: the extension beyond pure tensors needs an argument at the archimedean places (E39).

items.name: Beuzart-Plessis: local Plancherel formulas and matching of relative characters
items.statement: (Beuzart-Plessis, 'Plancherel formula for GL_n(F)∖GL_n(E) and applications to the Ichino–Ikeda and formal degree conjectures for unitary groups', Invent. Math. 2021; notation of its Theorem 5.4.1) For each local field F_v, extended to F_□ for a finite set □ of places containing the archimedean ones by taking products over v ∈ □ and by continuity (tensor products of local Schwartz spaces are dense, Aizenbud–Gourevitch Cor. 2.6.3): (a) ((5.5.10), giving (4.8)) ∫_{B′_rs(F_□)} O_η(γ, f′_1) conj(O_η(γ, f′_2)) dγ = |τ|_{E_□}^{−n(n−1)/2} ∫_{Temp(G^{qs}_□)/stab} I_{BC(π)}(f′_1) conj(I_{BC(π)}(f′_2)) |γ*(0, π, Ad, ψ′)|/|S_π| dπ for f′_1, f′_2 ∈ S(G′(F_□)); (b) ((5.5.3), giving (4.9)) ∫_{B^V_rs(F_□)} O(δ^V, f^V_1) conj(O(δ^V, f^V_2)) dδ^V = ∫_{Temp_{H^V_□}(G^V_□)} J_π(f^V_1) conj(J_π(f^V_2)) μ*_{G^V_□}(π) dπ for f^V_1, f^V_2 ∈ S(G^V(F_□)); (c) (Theorem 5.4.1) if f′ and (f^W)_W have matching orbital integrals, then κ_W J_π(f^W) = I_{BC(π)}(f′) for every W and every π ∈ Temp_{H^W}(G^W); (d) (Theorem 5.4.3) under the local Jacquet–Langlands map Temp_{H^V_□}(G^V_□) → Temp(G^{qs}_□)/stab the measure |γ*(0, π, Ad, ψ′)|/|S_π| dπ restricts to μ*_{G^V_□}(π) dπ; (e) κ_{V_□} conj(κ_{V_□}) = |τ|_{E_□}^{n(n−1)/2}; (f) (§5.7.3) the technique that separates π, turning an identity ∫_{Temp_{H^V_□}(G^V_□)} κ_{V_□}J_π(f^V) conj(J_π(g^V)) μ*(π) dπ = ∫ I_{BC(π)}(f′) conj(J_π(g^V)) μ*(π) dπ for all g^V ∈ ⊗_{v∈□} S_tr(G^V(F_v)) into the pointwise equality κ_{V_□}J_π(f^V) = I_{BC(π)}(f′). Here J_π, I_{BC(π)} are the local relative characters (local analogues of (4.3), (4.1)), which depend linearly on π(f^V) and BC(π)(f′).
items.note: At primes inert in E this relies on Mok and Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White (Remark 4.10).

items.name: Lemma 4.9: matching orbital integrals versus matching relative characters
items.statement: Let □ be a finite set of places of F containing all archimedean places and such that every prime in □ is split in E, and let V ∈ 𝔙. For f′ ∈ S(G′(F_□)) and f^V ∈ S(G^V(F_□)), f′ and f^V have matching orbital integrals (Definition 4.4(1)) if and only if they have matching relative characters, that is, κ_{V_□} J_π(f^V) = I_{BC(π)}(f′) for every π ∈ Temp_{H^V_□}(G^V_□). The notation is that of Beuzart-Plessis (Invent. Math. 2021, Theorem 5.4.1): Temp_{H^V_□}(G^V_□) is the set of tempered irreducible representations of G^V(F_□) distinguished by H^V(F_□); κ_{V_□} = ∏_{v∈□} κ_{V_v} is a constant depending only on V_□; J_π and I_{BC(π)} are the local relative characters, local analogues of (4.3) and (4.1), depending linearly on π(f^V) and BC(π)(f′).
items.note: Remark 4.10: the same holds for inert primes in □, using Mok and Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White.

items.name: Proposition 4.8: multipliers compatible with base change preserve smooth transfer
items.statement: Let S, K′ = K′_S × ∏_{v∉S}K′_v, V ∈ 𝔙, K^V = K^V_S × ∏_{v∉S}K^V_v (relative hyperspecial components outside S), T = S ∪ T_0 and bc^V be as in the setup of §4.2. Let f′ = ⊗_v f′_v ∈ S(G′(A_F))_{K′} and f^V = ⊗_v f^V_v ∈ S(G^V(A_F))_{K^V} be pure tensors such that f′_v and f^V_v have matching orbital integrals for every place v of F, and let μ′ and μ^V be T-multipliers of S(G′(A_F))_{K′} and S(G^V(A_F))_{K^V} (Definition 3.5) with μ^V = bc^V(μ′). Then μ′⋆f′ and μ^V⋆f^V are smooth transfer in the sense of Definition 4.4(2).

items.name: Proposition 4.11: Gaussian test functions at compact archimedean places
items.statement: At an archimedean place v nonsplit in E with V_v positive definite, S_tr(G^{V_v}(F_v)) contains every f^{V_v}_v with J_{π_v}(f^{V_v}_v) = 0 for all but finitely many tempered π_v.
items.note: Not used in the paper; it gives the Gaussian test functions of Rapoport–Smithling–Zhang. The proof writes J_{π_0}(f^V) = 1 for J_{π_0}(f^V_1) = 1 (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Lemma 4.12: choosing T-multipliers compatible under base change
items.statement: Setup of §4.3: S is a finite set of primes of F containing those ramified in E, T = S ∪ T_0 (T_0 the primes of F nonsplit in E), K′ ⊆ G′(A_F^∞) and K^V ⊆ G^V(A_F^∞) are as in §4.2, 𝔙°_(S) is a nonempty subset of 𝔙_(S), χ′ is a T-character of G′, and for each V ∈ 𝔙°_(S), χ^V is a T-character of G^V whose base change (via bc^V of (4.5)–(4.7)) is χ′. Lemma 4.12: given a T-multiplier μ′ of S(G′(A_F))_{K′} with μ′(χ′) = 1 and, for each V ∈ 𝔙°_(S), a T-multiplier μ^V of S(G^V(A_F))_{K^V} with μ^V(χ^V) = 1, there are T-multipliers μ̃′ of S(G′(A_F))_{K′} and μ̃^V of S(G^V(A_F))_{K^V} (V ∈ 𝔙°_(S)) such that (1) μ̃′(χ′) = 1 and μ̃′ = μ′·ν′ for some T-multiplier ν′ of S(G′(A_F))_{K′}; (2) for every V ∈ 𝔙°_(S), μ̃^V(χ^V) = 1, μ̃^V = μ^V·ν^V for some T-multiplier ν^V of S(G^V(A_F))_{K^V}, and μ̃^V = bc^V(μ̃′). (Proof: μ̃′ = (μ′)²·∏_{V∈𝔙°_(S)} cb^V((μ^V)²) and μ̃^V = bc^V(μ̃′), where cb^V = cb^V_∞ ⊗ cb^T_V is a linear section of bc^V, cb^T_V any linear section of bc^T_V and cb^V_∞(φ) = φ∘ℓ_V for a linear splitting ℓ_V : h′* → h^{V*} of h^{V*} ⊆ h′* sending W′-orbits into W^V-orbits; cb^V_∞ and bc^V_∞ preserve the moderate-growth spaces M, and Remark 2.9(3) gives M·M^♯ ⊆ M^♯.)

items.name: The Burger–Sarnak trick for U(n) × U(n+1) periods (W. Zhang, Proposition 2.14)
items.statement: (W. Zhang, Ann. of Math. 180 (2014), Proposition 2.14; as used) Let V = (V_n, V_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔙, let π_{n+1} ∈ ℭ(G^V_{n+1}, 1) be cuspidal automorphic, and let v_0 be a prime of F split in E at which π_{n+1,v_0} is generic. Then there is π_n ∈ ℭ(G^V_n, 1) with π_{n,v_0} supercuspidal such that the period 𝒫(φ) = ∫_{H^V(F)∖H^V(A_F)} φ(h) dh is nonzero on some cuspidal automorphic form φ ∈ L²(G^V, π_n ⊠ π_{n+1}). (In the proof of Theorem 4.14(2) v_0 is a prime at which π_{n+1,v_0} is supercuspidal; in the proof of Theorem 1.9 π_{n+1} is the descent of Lemma 4.16.)
items.locator: §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.14, p. 40; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.9, p. 42

items.name: Flicker: distinction and poles of Asai L-functions
items.statement: (Flicker, Bull. SMF 116 (1988)) A cuspidal Π of GL_m(A_E) has a nonzero period over GL_m(A_F) twisted by η^{m+1}_{E/F} iff L(s, Π, As^{(−1)^{m+1}}) has a pole at s = 1.
items.locator: §4.3, proof of Proposition 4.13, p. 39; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.8, p. 41

items.name: Strong multiplicity one for GL_n with a density-zero exceptional set
items.statement: (Ramakrishnan, arXiv:1806.08429, Theorem A) Isobaric automorphic representations of GL_n(A_E) that agree at the places above almost all primes of F split in E are isomorphic.
items.locator: §1.2, Definition 1.6, p. 4; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.8, p. 41
items.note: PAPER-GAN-SAVIN-23-B routed Jacquet–Shalika's strong multiplicity one to LocalLanglandsCorrespondenceForG2; the review should give strong multiplicity one for GL_n one owner.

items.name: Proposition 4.13: weak base change from nonvanishing periods
items.statement: Let S be a finite set of primes of F containing those ramified in E, T = S ∪ T_0, V ∈ 𝔙_(S) and π^V ∈ ℭ(G^V, 1). Suppose that some cuspidal automorphic form φ ∈ L²(G^V, π^V) satisfies 𝒫(φ) := ∫_{H^V(F)∖H^V(A_F)} φ(h) dh ≠ 0 (dh the Tamagawa measure on H^V(A_F)), and assume either (a) π^V is not (G^V, T)-CAP (Definition 3.4), or (b) there is a prime v_0 of F split in E such that π^V_{v_0} is supercuspidal. Then the weak automorphic base change of π^V (Definition 1.6) exists as an isobaric automorphic representation Π = BC(π^V) = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} of G′(A_F) = GL_n(A_E) × GL_{n+1}(A_E), and (1) the base change of χ_{π^V_∞} is χ_{Π_∞}; (2) in situation (b), Π_m is cuspidal and hermitian (Definition 1.5) for m = n, n+1.
items.note: The proof of (1) as written covers only the case where Π is cuspidal (sourceIssues E1); Theorem 3.19 closes it.

items.name: Theorem 4.14: weak base change for unitary groups without endoscopy
items.statement: Let V° be a hermitian space over E, G° = U(V°), and π = ⊗_v π_v an irreducible admissible representation of G°(A_F). (1) If π is cuspidal automorphic and π_v is generic for infinitely many primes v of F split in E, then the weak automorphic base change BC(π) exists. (2) If π is cuspidal automorphic and π_v is supercuspidal for some prime v of F split in E, then BC(π) exists and is cuspidal and hermitian (Definition 1.5). (3) If BC(π) exists and is hermitian, then π is not (G•, T_0)-CAP (Definition 3.4) for any pure inner form G• of G°. (4) If π is cuspidal automorphic and BC(π) exists and is hermitian, then the base change of χ_{π_∞} is χ_{BC(π)_∞}. [In print (4) lacks 'π is cuspidal automorphic'; as printed it is false, see E45.]
items.locator: §4.3, Theorem 4.14 and proof, pp. 39–40; Remarks 1.7 and 4.15
items.note: By induction on rank with the Burger–Sarnak trick and Proposition 4.13; independent of the endoscopic classification (which also implies it). (3) is consistent with Jiang's CAP conjecture. (4) rests on Proposition 4.13(1) (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Lemma 4.16: descent of hermitian representations to quasi-split unitary groups
items.statement: For a hermitian isobaric Π of GL_m(A_E) and V of rank m with U(V) quasi-split, there is a cuspidal π of U(V)(A_F) which is unramified at the split primes where Π is, with base change of χ_{π_v} equal to χ_{Π_v} there; hence Π ≅ BC(π) and the base change of χ_{π_∞} is χ_{Π_∞}.
items.note: Existence by the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent; the archimedean statement by Theorem 4.14(4).

items.name: The Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry automorphic descent
items.statement: (Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry, 2011) The descent from GL_m to classical and unitary groups constructs, for a hermitian isobaric Π, a cuspidal automorphic representation of the quasi-split unitary group whose unramified components correspond to those of Π.
items.note: ML.5 registers the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent among known transfers (as TwistedAutomorphicDescents, from PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20, imports it).

items.name: Rankin–Selberg periods and central values for GL_n × GL_{n+1}
items.statement: (Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika) For cuspidal Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1}, the H′_1-period ∫_{H′_1(F)∖H′_1(A_F)} φ is the Rankin–Selberg zeta integral at s = ½; some cusp form with prescribed unramified components has nonzero period iff L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0.
items.note: AL.3 plans the GL_n × GL_m Rankin–Selberg integrals with their unfolding and unramified computation.

items.name: The endoscopic classification of unitary groups
items.statement: (Mok; Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White) The endoscopic classification of representations of quasi-split unitary groups and their inner forms, used for generic packets in the proof of Theorem 1.10 and for Lemma 4.9 at inert primes.
items.locator: §4.2, Remark 4.10, p. 36; §4.3, Remark 4.15, p. 40; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.10, p. 43
items.note: ML.4 owns the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs.

items.name: Remark 4.17: Theorem 1.8 (1) ⇒ (2) with archimedean compatibility and relative hyperspecial fixed vectors
items.statement: Let Π_n and Π_{n+1} be hermitian cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n(A_E) and GL_{n+1}(A_E) with L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0. Then there are a hermitian space V_n of rank n (V_{n+1} = V_n ⊕ E·e, e of norm 1), irreducible subrepresentations π_m ⊆ A_cusp(G_m), G_m = U(V_m), with BC(π_m) ≅ Π_m, and cusp forms φ_m ∈ π_m (m = n, n+1) with 𝒫(φ_n, φ_{n+1}) ≠ 0 such that moreover: (i) the base change of χ_{π_{m,∞}} is χ_{Π_{m,∞}} for m = n, n+1; (ii) φ_n ⊗ φ_{n+1} is fixed by a relative hyperspecial maximal subgroup of G^V(F_v) (Definition 4.3) at every prime v of F that is unramified in E and at which Π_{n,v} ⊗ Π_{n+1,v} is unramified.
items.locator: §4.4, Remark 4.17, p. 42 (established in the proof of Theorem 1.8, pp. 41–42)

items.name: Remark 2.11: Schwartz functions versus Harish-Chandra L^p-Schwartz functions
items.statement: For G = G(R), G connected reductive over R: S(G) ⊆ ∩_{p>0} 𝒞^p(G), where 𝒞^p(G) is the convolution algebra of Harish-Chandra L^p-Schwartz functions on G. The inclusion is an equality if and only if the centre of G is compact.
items.note: Split from item 10. Not used in any proof. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.12: L²-Sobolev description of S(G) and its topology
items.statement: Let G = G(R), G connected reductive over R. By the Sobolev lemma, S(G) is the space of f ∈ L²(G) such that Df ∈ L²(G) (in the sense of distributions) for every algebraic differential operator D ∈ 𝒟(G). Moreover, the Fréchet topology of S(G) is induced by the semi-norms f ↦ ‖Df‖_{L²}, D ∈ 𝒟(G).
items.locator: §2.3, Remark 2.12, p. 12; used in §1.3, p. 5 ('a crucial observation') and in the proof of Proposition 2.24, p. 17
items.note: Split from item 10. It is the key input for extending μ⋆ by continuity from C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} to S(G). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Definition 3.1: Schwartz test functions on G(A_F)
items.statement: For a connected reductive group G over a number field F with fixed Haar measure dg = ∏_v dg_v on G(A_F), put G_∞ := G(F ⊗_Q R). The space of Schwartz test functions is S(G(A_F)) := S(G_∞) ⊗ S(G(A_F^∞)), an algebraic tensor product over C, with convolution for dg. Here S(G(A_F^∞)) = ⊗′_{v∤∞} S(G(F_v)) is the restricted tensor product, and S(G(F_v)) = C_c^∞(G(F_v)). For K = K_S × ∏_{v∉S} K_{0,v} as in §3.1, S(G(A_F))_K := S(G_∞) ⊗ S(G(A_F^∞))_K, the bi-K-invariant functions. S(G(A_F)) acts continuously on L²(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω) through R.
items.locator: §3.1, Definition 3.1, p. 21 (and p. 22 for S(G(A_F))_K); §1.4, p. 8 for G_∞
items.note: Split from item 10. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Delorme (1984): multipliers of C_c^∞(G) and C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} are polynomial, respectively of exponential type
items.statement: (Delorme, Invent. Math. 75 (1984), 9–23, final remark; as cited) Let G be a real semisimple Lie group without compact factors. The only W-invariant holomorphic functions μ on h*_C that give continuous multipliers μ⋆ of C_c^∞(G) with π(μ⋆f) = μ(χ_π)π(f) are the polynomials, i.e. the elements of the centre of U(g). For the subalgebra C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} of bi-K-finite functions (K a maximal compact subgroup), the W-invariant holomorphic functions that give continuous multipliers must be of exponential type.
items.note: Split from item 39. The paper attributes the first claim to the final remark of [Del84]; the second is stated in the same passage without its own citation. The result is motivational: it explains Remark 1.2(3) and footnote 3 (p. 6) and is not used in any proof. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Jacquet–Shalika classification: cuspidal data of GL_n are determined by almost all local components
items.statement: (Jacquet–Shalika, Amer. J. Math. 103 (1981), Theorem 4.4; as used) Let F′ be a number field. For i = 1, 2, let P_i be a parabolic subgroup of GL_n over F′ with Levi quotient M_i ≅ GL_{n_{i,1}} × ⋯ × GL_{n_{i,r_i}}, and let σ_i = σ_{i,1} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ σ_{i,r_i} be a cuspidal automorphic representation, not necessarily unitary, of M_i(A_{F′}). Suppose that for almost all places v the unramified constituents of Ind_{P_1}^{GL_n}(σ_{1,v}) and Ind_{P_2}^{GL_n}(σ_{2,v}) are isomorphic. Then r_1 = r_2 and (σ_{2,j})_j is a permutation of (σ_{1,j})_j. Equivalently, for G = Res_{F′/F} GL_n a cuspidal datum (M, σ) is determined up to equivalence by the spherical components, at almost all places, of any constituent of Ind_P^G(σ).
items.locator: §1.1, before Theorem 1.3, p. 2; §3.4, after Theorem 3.19, p. 29 (there cited as 'the strong multiplicity one property for G = Res_{F′/F} GL_n [PS79]'); also §1.1, before Theorem 1.3, p. 3 (cited as [JS81, Theorem 4.4]); §3.4, after Theorem 3.19, p. 29 (cited as 'strong multiplicity one … [PS79]')
items.note: This is the black-box input that turns Theorem 3.19 into Theorem 1.3: it makes 𝔇(G, ω)^♥_χ a single cuspidal datum for χ = χ_{π^S}. Strong multiplicity one for cuspidal representations alone ([PS79]) does not suffice for non-cuspidal π. The exact hypotheses in JS81 (twists allowed, isomorphism versus common constituent) should be checked against the source. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Isobaric automorphic representations of GL_n(A_E)
items.statement: For cuspidal automorphic representations Π_1, …, Π_d of GL_{n_1}(A_E), …, GL_{n_d}(A_E) with n_1 + ⋯ + n_d = n, the isobaric sum Π_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ Π_d is the automorphic representation of GL_n(A_E) whose component at each place w is the Langlands quotient of the normalised induction I_P^{GL_n}(Π_{1,w} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ Π_{d,w}), P standard of type (n_1, …, n_d). For unitary Π_i this induction is already irreducible. An isobaric automorphic representation is one of this form (Langlands; Jacquet–Shalika). By [JS81] it determines the multiset {Π_1, …, Π_d}.
items.note: Used without definition in Definitions 1.5–1.6 and Lemma 4.16. Standard (Langlands, 'On the notion of an automorphic representation'; Jacquet–Shalika 1981). Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Lattices and full lattices in a finite-dimensional complex vector space (§1.4)
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional complex vector space U, a lattice (resp. full lattice) of U is a subgroup L of U such that the induced map L ⊗_Z C → U is injective (resp. bijective).
items.note: Nonstandard: a Z-basis of a lattice must be C-linearly independent, so e.g. Z + iZ ⊂ C is not a lattice. Corollary 2.6 (lattice L ⊆ U_C, item 13) depends on this. With the usual real-lattice notion it would fail: a function vanishing on Z + iZ grows like exp(c|z|²) and cannot have moderate vertical growth. Also used in the proof of Lemma 3.14 (the lattice L_M ⊂ 𝔠*_{M,C}/𝔞*_{M,C}). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: O(U), O_exp(U) and C[U] (§1.4)
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional complex vector space U: O(U) is the ring of holomorphic functions on U; O_exp(U) ⊆ O(U) is the subring of holomorphic functions of exponential type (|μ(z)| ≤ C e^{A‖z‖} for some C, A > 0; the paper does not spell this out); C[U] ⊆ O_exp(U) is the subring of polynomial functions.
items.note: O_exp(h*_C)^W ⊗ H_G^T contains the 'mixed' element ν† in the proof of Proposition 3.17 (pp. 28–29). The multiplier bounds for C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} in §1.1 are phrased in terms of exponential type. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Unipotent radical N_P and normalised parabolic induction I_P^G (§1.4)
items.statement: For a parabolic subgroup P of a reductive group G, N_P ⊆ P is its unipotent radical. For an admissible representation σ of P(R), with R a ring for which admissibility makes sense, I_P^G(σ) is the normalised parabolic induction, an admissible representation of G(R). For an admissible representation σ of M(R), M a Levi subgroup of P, I_P^G(σ) is defined by inflating σ to P(R).
items.note: Used in Definition 3.5 (CAP) and throughout §3. The CAP conditions in Theorem 1.1 and Definition 3.5 do not depend on normalised versus unnormalised induction, because σ ranges over non-unitary cuspidal representations as well (δ_P^{1/2} is an automorphic character of M(A_F)). Planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans normalized parabolic induction for p-adic groups; AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.1 plans normalized induction from rational parabolics for cuspidal data.

items.name: Order of an entire function; the Weierstrass product Ψ_{Λ,p}
items.statement: The order of an entire function Ψ : C → C is inf{e ∈ [0, +∞) : there is C_e > 0 with |Ψ(z)| < C_e·exp(|z|^e) for all z ∈ C} (Ψ has infinite order if the set is empty). For Λ ⊆ C and an integer p ≥ 0, the (formal) Weierstrass product is Ψ_{Λ,p}(z) := z^δ·∏_{λ∈Λ, λ≠0} E_p(z/λ), where E_p(z) := (1 − z)·exp(z + z²/2 + ⋯ + z^p/p) and δ = 1 if 0 ∈ Λ, δ = 0 otherwise.
items.note: Unnumbered definitions used in Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.4. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: the Weierstrass product of a set of rank p
items.statement: Let Λ ⊆ C be a subset of rank p for some integer p ≥ 0. Then Ψ_{Λ,p} is a well-defined entire function of (finite) order at most p + 1, whose set of zeros is exactly Λ.
items.note: Previously bundled in item 12. Proof: the 'well-known' bound |Ψ_{Λ,p}(z)| < C·exp(C′|z|^{p+1}), which follows from log|E_p(z)| ≤ A_p|z|^{p+1}. Classical (Weierstrass–Hadamard); checked. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 2.4: functions of moderate vertical growth with zero set λ^{−1}(Ψ^{−1}(0))
items.statement: Let U be a finite-dimensional real vector space and λ : U_C → C a polynomial function. For every entire function Ψ of finite order there is a holomorphic function ν on U_C of moderate vertical growth whose set of zeros is exactly the inverse image under λ of the set of zeros of Ψ.
items.note: Previously bundled in item 13. Proof: U ≅ R^r, Ψ of order e, deg λ = d, q an odd integer > de, ν(z) = exp(z_1^{2q} + ⋯ + z_r^{2q})·Ψ(λ(z)). Checked: since q is odd, Re z_j^{2q} = −(Im z_j)^{2q} + O_M((1+|Im z_j|)^{2q−2}) on ‖Re z‖ < M, and |Ψ(λ(z))| ≤ C exp(C(1+‖z‖)^{de′}) with de′ < 2q. So ν even decays like exp(−c‖Im z‖^{2q}) on vertical strips. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Corollary 2.5: functions of moderate vertical growth vanishing exactly on λ^{−1}Λ
items.statement: Let U be a finite-dimensional real vector space and λ : U_C → C a polynomial function. For every subset Λ ⊆ C of finite rank there is a holomorphic function ν on U_C of moderate vertical growth whose set of zeros is exactly λ^{−1}Λ.
items.note: From Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.4. Used in §3.3 (p. 26) to build μ_∞. Previously bundled in item 13. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Corollary 2.6: vanishing on a lattice outside a finite set
items.statement: Let U be a finite-dimensional real vector space, L a lattice of U_C (a subgroup with L ⊗_Z C → U_C injective, §1.4; it must be finitely generated, see E15) and A ⊆ U_C a finite subset. Then there is a holomorphic function ν on U_C of moderate vertical growth that vanishes on L ∖ A and is nowhere zero on A.
items.note: Previously bundled in item 13. Proof: C-linear λ_1, …, λ_r with L ⊆ ∩ λ_i^{−1}Z; ν_i from Corollary 2.5 with zero set λ_i^{−1}(Z ∖ λ_i(A)); then ∏ν_i times affine factors l_j killing the finitely many remaining points of L ∖ A. Checked. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.7: exponential decay on vertical strips can be arranged
items.statement: From the proof of Proposition 2.4, the functions ν in Corollaries 2.5 and 2.6 may moreover be chosen to have exponential decay on vertical strips.
items.note: Not used later ('we do not need this in what follows'). Printed with μ for ν (E2). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.9(1): meaning of the growth conditions of Definition 2.8
items.statement: In Definition 2.8(1) (resp. (2)), for every ϑ ∈ θ and every ϖ ∈ Y*_ϑ, the function α ↦ μ(α + ϖ) on h*_{ϑ,C} has moderate vertical growth (resp. rapid decay on vertical strips). Restricted to i h*_ϑ ⊕ Y*_ϑ, the growth condition (2.1) says that μ has polynomial growth there.
items.note: Previously bundled in item 14. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.9(2): M_θ, N_θ and M^♯_θ are W-stable algebras
items.statement: The spaces M_θ(h*_C), N_θ(h*_C) and M^♯_θ(h*_C) are closed under multiplication and under the action of W.
items.note: Previously bundled in item 14. W-stability uses that θ is W-stable, that w(h*_{ϑ}) = h*_{wϑw^{−1}}, and that w(Y*_ϑ) = Y*_{wϑw^{−1}} since wρ + X* = ρ + X*. Used in the proof of Lemma 2.10. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.9(3): M^♯_θ is a module over functions of moderate vertical growth
items.statement: If μ ∈ O(h*_C) has moderate vertical growth, then μ·M^♯_θ(h*_C) ⊆ M^♯_θ(h*_C). In particular M(h*_C)·M^♯_θ(h*_C) ⊆ M^♯_θ(h*_C), where M(h*_C) = M_{{1}}(h*_C).
items.note: Previously bundled in item 14. Used in §3.3 (pp. 26, 29) and §4.3 (p. 37). Checked: on the finitely many non-vanishing translates h*_{ϑ,C} + ϖ, the strip ‖Re α‖ < M lies in the strip ‖Re‖ < M + ‖ϖ‖ of h*_C. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The set θ attached to a real reductive group
items.statement: Let G be a connected reductive group over R, and (X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨) the root datum of G_C: X* and X_* are the weight and coweight lattices of the abstract Cartan group of G_C, and Φ, Φ^∨ its roots and coroots. θ is the subset of Aut(X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨)^♡ of elements of the form wϑ with w ∈ W and ϑ ∈ Aut^♡ an element inducing the real form G of G_C. θ is stable under W-conjugation.
items.note: Used in Theorem 2.13, throughout §2.4 and in §3. Item 17 mentions θ only inside the theorem. The proof of Lemma 2.21 (p. 15) uses the special form of θ: if ϑ ∈ θ, w ∈ W and (wϑ)² = 1, then wϑ ∈ θ. θ lies in a single coset Wϑ, so it is finite; this is what the later max over θ needs, since Aut^♡ itself can be infinite (E16). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The abstract Cartan group H and universal isomorphisms
items.statement: The abstract Cartan group H of G_C represents the functor on complex tori S ↦ {families (q_B : B → S)_B of homomorphisms, B running over the Borel subgroups of G_C, with q_B = q_{B′}∘α_{B,B′} for every inner automorphism α_{B,B′} of G_C mapping B into B′}; its weight lattice is X*. For every maximal torus T of G there is a canonical W-conjugacy class of isomorphisms T_C ≅ H, the universal isomorphisms. For T := T(R) = A_T T_c (maximal split and anisotropic sub-tori), with t = a_T ⊕ t_c, a universal isomorphism induces h* = a*_T ⊕ i t*_c.
items.note: Unnumbered; used in Lemma 2.19, Remark 2.14 (θ_G) and the proof of Proposition 2.24. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The seminorms p_{ϑ,M,r}
items.statement: Fix a W-invariant Euclidean norm ‖·‖ on h*_C. For ϑ ∈ Aut(X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨)^♡, M > 0, r ∈ R and μ ∈ O(h*_C), p_{ϑ,M,r}(μ) := sup_{α∈h*_{ϑ,C}, ‖Re α‖<M, ϖ∈Y*_ϑ} |μ(α+ϖ)|·(1 + ‖α+ϖ‖)^r ∈ [0, ∞]. Then p_{ϑ,M,r}(μ) ≤ p_{ϑ,M′,r}(μ) if M ≤ M′, and p_{ϑ,M,r}(μ) ≤ p_{ϑ,M,r′}(μ) if r ≤ r′.
items.note: Used in Lemmas 2.20–2.21, Proposition 2.24 and the proof of Theorem 2.13. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The extended affine Weyl group W̃, the functions ℓ_s and the algebras ℛ ⊆ 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒯
items.statement: W̃ := X* ⋊ W is the extended affine Weyl group, acting on h*_C by affine maps. W̃^♡ ⊆ W̃ is its set of reflections, the s ∈ W̃ whose fixed locus H_s in h*_C is an affine hyperplane; for each s ∈ W̃^♡ fix an affine function ℓ_s on h*_C with zero locus H_s. For w ∈ W̃, t_w is the operator on C[h*_C] with (t_wP)(α) = P(w^{−1}α). ℛ is the algebra of endomorphisms of C[h*_C] generated by the t_w (w ∈ W̃) and by multiplication by elements of C[h*_C], viewed as a left C[h*_C]-module. 𝒮 := C[h*_C][ℓ_s^{−1} | s ∈ W̃^♡] ⊗_{C[h*_C]} ℛ and 𝒯 := C(h*_C) ⊗_{C[h*_C]} ℛ, with natural algebra maps ℛ → 𝒮 → 𝒯. 𝒮 does not depend on the choice of the ℓ_s, and 𝒯 is the algebra of endomorphisms of C(h*_C) generated by the t_w and by multiplication by elements of C(h*_C).
items.note: Previously part of the setup of item 22. Used in Lemmas 2.20, 2.22, 2.23 and Proposition 2.24. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemma 2.21: dividing by ℓ_s preserves the seminorm bounds
items.statement: (G, θ as in §2.3.) For every s ∈ W̃^♡ there is M_s > 0 such that for every M > 0 and every r ∈ R there is C_{s,M,r} > 0 with p_{1,M,r}(ℓ_s^{−1}μ) ≤ C_{s,M,r}·p_{1,M+M_s,r}(μ) and max_{ϑ∈θ} p_{ϑ,M,r}(ℓ_s^{−1}μ) ≤ C_{s,M,r}·max_{ϑ∈θ} p_{ϑ,M+M_s,r}(μ) for every μ ∈ O(h*_C) vanishing on H_s. In particular, if μ ∈ N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C) vanishes on H_s, then ℓ_s^{−1}μ ∈ N_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C).
items.note: Previously bundled in item 22; item 22's note about E4 belongs here. Proof, checked. If ℓ°_s is nonzero on h*_{ϑ,C}, use the mean-value estimate (2.2). Otherwise ϑ ≠ 1 and ϑ(β) = −β for the root β of w_s, so ϑ′ = w_sϑ is an involution in θ, with h*^−_{ϑ′} = h*^−_ϑ ∩ ker ℓ°_s and h*_ϑ ⊆ h*_{ϑ′}. Off H_s the bound is (2.3), since ℓ_s(h*_{ϑ,C} ⊕ Y*_ϑ) is discrete. On H_s, apply (2.2) for ϑ′, using proj_{h*^−_{ϑ′}}(Y*_ϑ) = Y*_{ϑ′}. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemma 2.23: elements of 𝒯 preserving polynomials come from 𝒮
items.statement: If T ∈ 𝒯 satisfies T(C[h*_C]) ⊆ C[h*_C], then T lies in the image of 𝒮 → 𝒯.
items.locator: §2.4, Lemma 2.23 and proof, p. 17; also §2.4, Lemma 2.23 and proof, p. 17
items.note: Previously bundled in item 22. The paper says it is 'essentially [KK86, Lemma 4.9]' and proves it: for an irreducible P not in any ℓ_sC[h*_C], a generic point of Z(P) has trivial stabiliser in W̃, and the evaluations Q ↦ Q(w^{−1}α) are independent, so P divides every P_w. Used in the proof of Lemma 2.22, which precedes it. The proof, on p. 17, was checked. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Example 2.15: the spaces of multiplier functions for real forms of SL_2
items.statement: Let G_C = SL_{2,C}: X* = Z, Φ = {2, −2}, W = Aut(X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨) = {±1}. (1) If G is split, θ = θ_G = {±1} and M_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W = M_{θ_G}(h*_C)^W = M_{{±1}}(h*_C)^W, which consists of the even holomorphic functions on C of moderate vertical growth with polynomial growth on Z ⊆ C. (2) If G is anisotropic, θ_G = {−1} ⊆ θ = {±1} and M_{θ_G}(h*_C)^W = M_{{−1}}(h*_C)^W, which consists of the even holomorphic functions on C with polynomial growth on Z ⊆ C.
items.note: Previously bundled in item 18. Checked: ρ = 1, so Y*_{−1} = 1 + Z = Z. Misprint 'identity' for 'identify' (E20). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.16: conjectural description of all multipliers μ⋆
items.statement: Conjecture: a holomorphic W-invariant function μ on h*_C gives a multiplier as in Theorem 2.13 if and only if μ ∈ M_{θ_G}(h*_C)^W. In particular there would be a homomorphism M_{θ_G}(h*_C)^W → Mul(S(G)) of complex algebras. The remark also says: 'By a result of Harish-Chandra', the set of infinitesimal characters of irreducible admissible representations of G is ∪_{ϑ∈θ_G} h*_{ϑ,C} ⊕ Y*_ϑ, so the kernel would consist exactly of the μ vanishing on this union; only the inclusion ⊆ holds (E19). The conjecture is easily checked for G anisotropic (G compact). For G split, Theorem 2.13 gives the homomorphism M_{θ_G}(h*_C)^W → Mul(S(G)), since then θ ∪ {1} = θ = θ_G. For G = SL_{2,R} the conjecture follows from Barker [Bar88].
items.note: Previously bundled in item 18. For split G, Theorem 2.13 proves only the 'if' direction; item 18 said the conjecture was 'known for G split'. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.17: the algebra homomorphism M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W → Mul(S(G))
items.statement: Theorem 2.13 and Definition 2.8(3) give a homomorphism of complex algebras M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W → Mul(S(G)), μ ↦ μ⋆.
items.note: Previously bundled in item 18. Uses M^♯_θ ⊆ M_{θ∪{1}}; multiplicativity follows from uniqueness in Theorem 2.13. Used in §3. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Kostant: the annihilating polynomial of δ(z)
items.statement: (Kostant, J. Funct. Anal. 20 (1975), Theorem 4.9) Let τ, δ and R_τ be as in Kostant's Theorem 4.8, identify Z(g) = C[h*_C]^W by the Harish-Chandra isomorphism, and let Λ(τ) ⊂ X* be the (W-stable) set of weights of τ. For z ∈ Z(g) put P_z(X) = ∏_{λ∈Λ(τ)} (X − z_{[λ]}) where z_{[λ]}(α) = z(α + λ). The coefficients of P_z lie in C[h*_C]^W = Z(g), and P_z(δ(z)) = 0 in R_τ, where Z(g) acts through z ↦ z ⊗ 1. The roots z_{[λ]}, λ ∈ Λ(τ), are pairwise distinct characters of Z(g).
items.note: Split from /23. The paper prints the roots as t_λ z, which with (t_wP)(α) = P(w^{-1}α) and the usual translation action of X* on h*_C is α ↦ z(α − λ). With that reading the identity has the wrong sign (E23). Only the facts that the roots are the translates by a finite W-stable subset of X* and that they are pairwise distinct are used. The set version (no multiplicities) is what is used, and it holds because δ(z) acts semisimply on M ⊗ W_τ for Verma modules M of generic infinitesimal character. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Harish-Chandra: infinitesimal characters of tempered representations
items.statement: (Harish-Chandra, J. Funct. Anal. 19 (1975)) For every irreducible tempered representation π of G, the infinitesimal character χ_π (a W-orbit in h*_C) meets ⋃_{ϑ∈θ_G} (i h*_ϑ ⊕ Y*_ϑ), where θ_G ⊆ θ is the W-stable set of involutions induced by the maximal tori of G (Lemma 2.19, Remark 2.14).
items.note: Split from /25. The paper claims equality ('the union of χ_π for π ∈ Temp(G) is exactly …'), which fails for G = SU(2) (E25). Only this inclusion is used, to bound |μ(χ_π)| by max_{ϑ∈θ_G} p_{ϑ,1,r}(μ)(1 + ‖χ_π‖)^{−r}. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 2.26: μ⋆ is continuous and preserves bi-K-finite functions
items.statement: For every μ ∈ M_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W, the operator μ⋆ : S(G) → S(G) of Theorem 2.13 is continuous and preserves the subalgebra S(G)_{(K)} of bi-K-finite functions in S(G). Moreover, the argument deducing Theorem 2.13 from Proposition 2.24, applied to Proposition A.1, shows that every element of M(h*_C)^W gives a multiplier of S(G)_{(K)}.
items.note: Item 17 is narrowed to Theorem 2.13, so the remark has its own item. The paper prints M_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C) and M(h*_C) without ^W (E27). The first sentence is used in the proof of Proposition 3.15 (p. 27). Continuity follows from the proof: μ⋆ is the pointwise limit of the maps μ_n⋆, each continuous by (2.4), and Banach–Steinhaus applies. The second sentence is not used later. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Harish-Chandra's subquotient theorem
items.statement: (Harish-Chandra; Casselman's subrepresentation theorem gives the stronger form) Every irreducible admissible representation of G is a subquotient of a principal series representation I_{P_0}^G(σ_ξ), where P_0 = M_0N_0 is a minimal parabolic subgroup, σ is an irreducible finite-dimensional representation of M_0 and ξ is an unramified character of M_0.
items.note: Used as a black box without citation ('By the subquotient theorem, it is enough to check (2.6) when π is a principal series'). The step also uses that principal series have an infinitesimal character, and it only needs the outer equality in (2.6). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Generic irreducibility of minimal principal series
items.statement: (Bruhat; Harish-Chandra) Let P_0 = M_0N_0 be a minimal parabolic subgroup of G and σ an irreducible representation of M_0. Then I_{P_0}^G(σ ⊗ ξ) is irreducible for ξ (an unramified character of M_0) in general position.
items.note: Used without citation in 'for generic ξ, the representations {I^G_{P_0}(V_λ ⊗ ξ)} are all semisimple': each V_λ is a finite direct sum of irreducible representations of M_0. The proof also uses the tensor identity I_{P_0}^G(σ_ξ) ⊗ τ ≅ I_{P_0}^G(σ_ξ ⊗ τ|_{P_0}), which the paper calls 'Frobenius reciprocity'. It is elementary and is not listed separately. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Definition 3.4: (G′, T)-CAP T-characters and representations
items.statement: Let G′ be an inner form of G over F. A T-character χ is (G′, T)-CAP if there exist a proper parabolic subgroup P′ of G′ and a cuspidal automorphic representation σ of M_{P′}(A_F), where M_{P′} := P′/N_{P′}, such that for all but finitely many primes v of F not in T for which G_v ≃ G′_v, the spherical representation corresponding to χ_v is a constituent of I^{G′}_{P′}(σ_v). An irreducible admissible representation π of G(A_F) is (G′, T)-CAP if χ_{π^T} is.
items.note: Split from the bundled item /29. After Piatetski-Shapiro's CAP representations [PS82]; §3 uses only G′ = G, §4 the general case. No unitarity is imposed on σ: the proof of Theorem 3.6 (p. 30) applies the definition to the non-unitary twists σ_s, s ∈ a*_{M,C}. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Definition 3.5: T-multipliers of S(G(A_F))_K
items.statement: Let (X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨) and θ ⊆ Aut(X*, Φ, X_*, Φ^∨)^♡ be attached to G ⊗_Q R as in §2.3, with h* = X* ⊗ R and M^♯_θ(h*_C) as in Definition 2.8. A T-multiplier of S(G(A_F))_K is an element of M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W ⊗ H_G^T. Such a μ (indeed any μ ∈ O(h*_C)^W ⊗ H_G^T) can be evaluated at a T-character χ to give μ(χ) ∈ C. Since Theorem 2.13 gives a linear map M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W → Mul(S(G_∞)) (Remark 2.17) and H_G^T is contained in the centre of S(G(A_F^∞))_K, a T-multiplier μ induces a multiplier μ⋆ ∈ Mul(S(G(A_F))_K).
items.locator: §3.1, Definition 3.5 and the adjacent paragraphs, pp. 22–23
items.note: Split from the bundled item /29. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The level-K spaces and the χ-part of the cuspidal spectrum
items.statement: Fix a set T of primes of F containing S_G and a T-character χ = (χ_∞, χ^{∞,T}), a finite set S of primes with S_G ⊆ S ⊆ T, and a subgroup K ⊆ K_0^∞ of finite index of the form K = K_S × ∏_{v∉S} K_{0,v}. S(G(A_F^∞))_K is the subalgebra of bi-K-invariant functions in S(G(A_F^∞)) and S(G(A_F))_K := S(G_∞) ⊗ S(G(A_F^∞))_K. For ? = ∅, cusp, L²_?(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) is the subspace of R(K)-invariant functions in L²_?(G(F)∖G(A_F), ω), on which S(G(A_F))_K acts continuously via R. L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)[χ] ⊆ L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) is the maximal closed subspace on whose smooth vectors Z(g) ⊗ H_G^T acts by the character χ_∞ ⊗ χ^{∞,T}.
items.note: Unnumbered; these are the standing data and spaces of Theorems 3.6, 3.7 and 3.19. The last sentence was inside the bundled item /29. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Definition 3.9: cuspidal data 𝔇(G, ω)^♡ (with the standard-Levi notation of §3.2)
items.statement: Fix a minimal Levi subgroup M_0 of G, a minimal parabolic P_0 ⊇ M_0, and a maximal torus T of G ⊗_Q R contained in M_0 ⊗_Q R (X* is identified with the weight lattice of T_C); K_0 is assumed admissible relative to M_0(A_F) [Art81, §1], and W(G, M_0) is the Weyl group of (G, M_0). A standard Levi subgroup M is the Levi subgroup containing M_0 of a parabolic subgroup containing P_0; P_M is that parabolic, Z_M the centre of M, Ω_M(ω) the set of unitary automorphic characters ω_M of Z_M(A_F) with ω_M|_{Z(A_F)} = ω, M(A_F)^1 the intersection of the kernels of all automorphic characters M(A_F) → R^×_+, and a_M the real vector space Z(A_F)M(A_F)^1∖M(A_F). For s ∈ a*_{M,C}, ξ_s: Z(A_F)M(A_F)^1∖M(A_F) → C^× is the character obtained by composing s with exp (unitary iff s ∈ i a*_M), and σ_s := σ ⊗ ξ_s for an admissible representation σ of M(A_F). Definition 3.9: for a cuspidal automorphic representation σ of M(A_F) with central character ω_M ∈ Ω_M(ω), L²(M, σ) ⊆ L²_cusp(M(F)∖M(A_F), ω_M) is the maximal closed σ-isotypic subspace. 𝔆(M, ω) is the set of isomorphism classes of cuspidal automorphic representations of M(A_F) whose central character lies in Ω_M(ω), with σ ∼ σ′ iff σ′ = σ_s for some s ∈ i a*_M, and 𝔆(M, ω)^♡ := 𝔆(M, ω)/∼. 𝔇(G, ω) is the set of pairs (M, σ) with M a standard Levi subgroup and σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω), with (M, σ) ≈ (M′, σ′) iff there is w ∈ W(G, M_0) with M′ = M^w and σ′ ∼ σ^w, and 𝔇(G, ω)^♡ := 𝔇(G, ω)/≈; its elements are called cuspidal data.
