items.note: Item /32 (the decomposition (3.1)) uses Definition 3.9 but no item states it. Footnote 6 (p. 23): a_M is Arthur's a_M^G (E28). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Maximal compact subgroups admissible relative to M_0 (Arthur)
items.statement: (Arthur, 'The trace formula in invariant form', Ann. of Math. 114 (1981), §1) The maximal compact subgroup K_0 = ∏_v K_{0,v} of G(A_F) may be taken admissible relative to M_0(A_F). Then for every standard Levi subgroup M: G(A_F) = N_{P_M}(A_F)M(A_F)K_0 (Iwasawa decomposition) with P_M(A_F) ∩ K_0 = (N_{P_M}(A_F) ∩ K_0)(M(A_F) ∩ K_0); K^M_{0,∞} := M_∞ ∩ K_{0,∞} is a maximal compact subgroup of M_∞; and M(F_v) ∩ K_{0,v} is a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of M(F_v) for every prime v at which K_{0,v} is hyperspecial.
items.locator: §3.2, p. 23 ('Without lost of generality…'); used in §3.2, p. 24 (Iwasawa decomposition in Φ̃), §3.3, p. 25 (K^M_{0,∞}, K_{M,v}) and §3.4, p. 28
items.note: Black-box input used without comment; the consequences listed are the ones the construction of 𝔗_M, K_M and the proofs of Propositions 3.15 and 3.17 rely on (e.g. I^G_{P_M}(σ_v)^{K_{0,v}} ≅ σ_v^{M(F_v)∩K_{0,v}}). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Remark 3.10: c*_M/a*_M as a cotangent space
items.statement: For a standard Levi subgroup M, c*_M/a*_M is canonically the real cotangent space of Z_M(A_F)^1 Z(A_F) at the identity; in particular the infinitesimal character of a character of Z_M(A_F)^1 Z(A_F) is an element of c*_{M,C}/a*_{M,C}. (The paper continues: 'Thus, c*_M = a*_M holds if and only if Z = 1 and Z_M(A_F)^1 is discrete; and c*_M = a*_M holds for every standard Levi subgroup M if and only if G is semisimple and split over Q.')
items.note: Split from the bundled item /35. Only the first sentence is used (proof of Lemma 3.14: the infinitesimal character of ω_{σ,∞} is γ_M^+(χ_{σ_s,∞})). The two quoted consequences are misstated (E30, E31): 'discrete' should be 'totally disconnected', and the last 'only if' fails for anisotropic G; correct form: c*_M = a*_M for all standard M iff G is semisimple and the identity component of the centre of Res_{F/Q}M_0 is Q-split. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The auxiliary types 𝔗, 𝔗_M, levels K_M and the sets 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M), 𝔆(M_der; K_{M_der}, 𝔗_{M_der})
items.statement: Choose μ^0_∞ ∈ M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W with μ^0_∞(χ_∞) ≠ 0 (Lemma 2.10) and let 𝔗 := 𝔗(μ^0_∞) be the finite set of K_{0,∞}-types of Lemma 2.18. For every standard Levi subgroup M of G: K^M_{0,∞} := M_∞ ∩ K_{0,∞}, a maximal compact subgroup of M_∞; 𝔗_M is a finite set of K^M_{0,∞}-types such that every irreducible admissible representation σ of M_∞ for which I^G_{P_M}(σ)|_{K_{0,∞}} contains a member of 𝔗 has σ|_{K^M_{0,∞}} containing a member of 𝔗_M (𝔗_G := 𝔗); K_{M,S} is an open compact subgroup of M(F_S) such that every irreducible admissible representation σ of M(F_S) with I^G_{P_M}(σ)^{K_S} ≠ {0} has σ^{K_{M,S}} ≠ {0} (K_{G,S} := K_S); K_{M,v} := M(F_v) ∩ K_v for primes v ∉ S (hyperspecial maximal in M(F_v)); K_M := K_{M,S} × ∏_{v∉S} K_{M,v}. 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M) is the set of σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω) with σ^{K_M} ≠ {0} and σ_∞|_{K^M_{0,∞}} containing a member of 𝔗_M; it is stable under ∼, with quotient 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M)^♡. Further K_{M_der} := K_M ∩ M_der(A_F^∞), K^{M_der}_{0,∞} := K^M_{0,∞} ∩ M_{der,∞}, 𝔗_{M_der} is the finite set of K^{M_der}_{0,∞}-types occurring in the restrictions of members of 𝔗_M, and 𝔆(M_der; K_{M_der}, 𝔗_{M_der}) is the set of isomorphism classes of cuspidal automorphic representations ς of M_der(A_F) with ς^{K_{M_der}} ≠ {0} and ς|_{K^{M_der}_{0,∞}} containing a member of 𝔗_{M_der}.
items.note: Unnumbered; used in Lemmas 3.12–3.14 and Propositions 3.15, 3.17. The existence of 𝔗_M (Frobenius reciprocity, I^G_{P_M}(σ)|_{K_{0,∞}} = Ind_{K^M_{0,∞}}^{K_{0,∞}}(σ|_{K^M_{0,∞}})) and of K_{M,S} (finitely many double cosets P_M(F_S)∖G(F_S)/K_S) is asserted without comment; both are standard. The paper writes K_∞ for K_{0,∞} in the definition of 𝔗_M (E33). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemma 3.13: finitely many χ_∞-typical cuspidal classes of bounded level and type
items.statement: For every standard Levi subgroup M of G, the set 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M)^♡ ∩ 𝔆(M, ω)^♡_{χ_∞} is finite.
items.note: Split from the bundled item /36. The printed proof uses only Donnelly's theorem for M_der and the Casimir condition; the γ_M^+ condition of Definition 3.11 and the passage from M_der back to M are needed but not argued (E35). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Lemma 3.14: archimedean multipliers killing the non-typical classes for a Levi M
items.statement: For every standard Levi subgroup M of G there exists μ^M_∞ ∈ M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W with μ^M_∞(χ_∞) ≠ 0 such that for every σ ∈ 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M)^♡ ∖ 𝔆(M, ω)^♡_{χ_∞}, μ^M_∞ vanishes on χ^G_{σ_s,∞}, the infinitesimal character of Ind^G_{P_M}(σ_{s,∞}), for every s ∈ a*_{M,C}.
items.note: Split from the bundled item /36. Proof: μ^M_∞ := μ^0_∞ ∏_{w∈W} ν∘w with ν = ν^+ × ν^− on c*_{M,C}/a*_{M,C} ⊕ b*_{M,C}, pulled back along h*_C → h*_C/a*_{M,C}; ν^− (Corollary 2.5, via Lemma 3.12) has zero set λ_M^{−1}(Λ(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M) ∖ λ_M(γ_M^−(χ_∞))); ν^+ (Corollary 2.6) vanishes on L_M ∖ γ_M^+(χ_∞) and not on γ_M^+(χ_∞), where L_M is a lattice containing every γ_M^+(χ_{σ_s,∞}) (compactness of Z_M(F)∖Z_M(A_F)^1/(K_M ∩ Z_M(A_F^∞)) and Remark 3.10); membership in M^♯_θ by Remark 2.9(3). Checked: correct. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 3.15: μ_∞ annihilates all but finitely many cuspidal components
items.statement: Let (3.3) be the surjection ∐_M 𝔆(M, ω)^♡ → 𝔇(G, ω)^♡ induced by the identification ∐_M 𝔆(M, ω) = 𝔇(G, ω); let 𝔇(G, ω; K, 𝔗)^♡ be the image of ∐_M 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M)^♡ and 𝔇(G, ω; K, 𝔗)^♡_{χ_∞} the image of ∐_M 𝔆(M, ω; K_M, 𝔗_M)^♡ ∩ 𝔆(M, ω)^♡_{χ_∞} (a finite set, by Lemma 3.13). Proposition 3.15: the function μ_∞ := μ^0_∞ · ∏_M μ^M_∞, the product over the standard Levi subgroups M of G with μ^M_∞ from Lemma 3.14, belongs to M^♯_θ(h*_C)^W and satisfies μ_∞(χ_∞) ≠ 0; moreover, for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K the endomorphism R(μ_∞⋆f) of L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) annihilates L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) whenever (M, σ) ∉ 𝔇(G, ω; K, 𝔗)^♡_{χ_∞}.
items.note: Split from the bundled item /36. Footnote 7: the product may be taken over representatives of standard Levi subgroups modulo W(G, M_0). Proof: reduce to bi-K_{0,∞}-finite f (Remark 2.26) and to pseudo-Eisenstein series, where Ind^G_{P_M}(σ_s)(μ_∞⋆f) = μ_∞(χ^G_{σ_s,∞})Ind^G_{P_M}(σ_s)(f); the three cases σ^{K_M} = 0, no 𝔗_M-type, non-typical are handled by K_M, 𝔗_M (with Lemma 2.18) and Lemma 3.14. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: The T-character χ^G_{σ_s^T} of an unramified cuspidal datum
items.statement: Let (M, σ) ∈ 𝔇(G, ω) with σ^{K_M} ≠ {0}. For every s ∈ a*_{M,C} and every prime v ∉ T, I^G_{P_M}(σ_{s,v})^{K_v} ≠ {0}, which gives a character χ^G_{σ_s,v}: H_{G,v} → C and hence a character χ^G_{σ_s^{∞,T}}: H_G^T → C; with χ^G_{σ_s,∞}, the infinitesimal character of I^G_{P_M}(σ_{s,∞}) (the W-orbit of χ_{σ_s,∞}), this gives a T-character χ^G_{σ_s^T} = (χ^G_{σ_s,∞}, χ^G_{σ_s^{∞,T}}) of G (superscript G suppressed when M = G). χ occurs in (M, σ) (Definition 3.16) iff χ = χ^G_{σ_s^T} for some s ∈ a*_{M,C}. For ν ∈ H_{G,v} (v ∉ T), and for ν ∈ C[h*_C]^W (v = ∞, H_{G,∞} := C[h*_C]^W), and any w′ ∈ W, the function α ↦ ν(χ^G_{σ_{ℓ(w′α)−ℓ(α_σ)},v}) on h*_C is of exponential type (ℓ: h* → a*_M a linear splitting, α_σ ∈ χ_{σ_∞}).
items.note: Unnumbered; the Satake-parameter bookkeeping behind Definition 3.16 and the mixed multiplier ν^† of Proposition 3.17. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 3.17: a T-multiplier annihilating a cuspidal component in which χ does not occur
items.statement: Let (M, σ) ∈ 𝔇(G, ω) and assume that χ does not occur in (M, σ). Then there exists a T-multiplier μ_{(M,σ)} of S(G(A_F))_K such that (1) for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K, the endomorphism R(μ_{(M,σ)}⋆f) of L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) annihilates L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω); (2) μ_{(M,σ)}(χ) ≠ 0.
items.note: Split from the bundled item /37. For M proper: fix α_σ ∈ χ_{σ_∞}, α_χ ∈ χ_∞ and a linear splitting ℓ: h* → a*_M; s_w := ℓ(wα_χ) − ℓ(α_σ); choose a place v[w] (∞ or a prime ∉ T) and ν_w ∈ H_{G,v[w]} with ν_w(χ_{v[w]}) ≠ ν_w(χ^G_{σ_{s_w},v[w]}) (3.4); ν^†_{w,w′} := ν_w − ν_w(χ^G_{σ_{ℓ∘w′(−)−ℓ(α_σ)},v[w]}); ν^† := ∏_{w′∈W} Σ_{w∈W} C_w ν^†_{w,w′} ∈ O_exp(h*_C)^W ⊗ H_G^T with ν^†(χ) ≠ 0 and ν^†(χ^G_{σ_s^T}) = 0 for all s; μ_{(M,σ)} := μ^0_∞ · μ^† · ν^† with μ^† ∈ M(h*_C)^W compensating the exponential growth (Remark 2.9(3)). Idea after Lindenstrauss–Venkatesh [LV07] (Remark 3.18). Checked: correct for M proper; the M = G case has a slip (E36). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Theorem 3.19: isolating the cuspidal components in which χ occurs
items.statement: Let χ be a T-character (standing data ω, T, S, K as in §3.1). There exists a T-multiplier μ of S(G(A_F))_K such that (1) for every f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K, the image of the endomorphism R(μ⋆f): L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) → L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) is contained in ⊕_{(M,σ)∈𝔇(G,ω)^♡_χ} L²_{(M,σ)}(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) under the decomposition (3.2), where 𝔇(G, ω)^♡_χ is as in Definition 3.16; (2) μ(χ) = 1.
items.note: Split from the bundled item /37; the main result of §3. Printed with '(3.9)' for (3.2) (sourceIssues E5). Proof: μ := μ(χ)^{−1} μ_∞ ∏_{(M,σ)∈𝔇} μ_{(M,σ)}, 𝔇 a finite set of representatives of 𝔇(G, ω; K, 𝔗)^♡_{χ_∞} ∖ 𝔇(G, ω)^♡_χ; the image in fact lies in the finite sum over 𝔇(G, ω; K, 𝔗)^♡_{χ_∞} ∩ 𝔇(G, ω)^♡_χ (𝔇(G, ω)^♡_χ itself need not be finite when T is infinite). Theorems 3.6 and 3.7 are deduced on p. 30 from L²_cusp(…/K, ω) ∩ ⊕̂_{𝔇(G,ω)^♡_χ} L²_{(M,σ)}(…/K, ω) = L²_cusp(…/K, ω)[χ] and, for 3.6, from the fact that a non-(G, T)-CAP χ occurs only in data with M = G; Theorem 1.3 by T = S, χ = χ_{π^T} and strong multiplicity one. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Proposition 4.2: Zydor's Jacquet–Rallis relative trace formula for G^V and quasi-cuspidal Schwartz functions
items.statement: (Zydor, J. reine angew. Math. 762 (2020), Théorème 6.7; the paper asserts that its proof works for Schwartz test functions) Let V ∈ 𝔙 and let f^V ∈ S(G^V(A_F)) be a quasi-cuspidal Schwartz test function (Definition 3.2, ω trivial). Then Σ_{π^V∈𝔆(G^V,1)} J_{π^V}(f^V) = Σ_{δ^V∈B^V(F)} J_{δ^V}(f^V), both sums being absolutely convergent.
items.note: Split off from item 44. The sentence introducing it says I_γ where J_{δ^V} is meant (sourceIssues E6). Used in the proofs of Proposition 4.13 and Theorem 1.8. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Schwartz algebras S(G(F_□)) and S(G(F_□))_K at a finite set of places
items.statement: For G ∈ {G′, G^V} and every finite set □ of places of F containing all archimedean ones, S(G(F_□)) := S(G_∞) ⊗ ⊗_{v∈□, v∤∞} S(G(F_v)), where S(G_∞) is the Schwartz algebra of G_∞ = G(F ⊗_Q R) and S(G(F_v)) = C_c^∞(G(F_v)) for v finite. Given relative hyperspecial (or other open compact) subgroups K′_v, K^V_v at the finite v ∈ □, S(G′(F_□))_{K′} and S(G^V(F_□))_{K^V} are the subalgebras of functions bi-invariant under ∏_{v∈□, v∤∞} K′_v, resp. ∏_{v∈□, v∤∞} K^V_v.
items.locator: §4.2, before Definition 4.4, p. 33; proof of Proposition 4.8, p. 35
items.note: Used in Definition 4.4, Lemma 4.9 and the proof of Proposition 4.8. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Definition 4.4(1): matching orbital integrals
items.statement: Let □ be a finite set of places of F containing all archimedean ones and V ∈ 𝔙. Then f′_□ ∈ S(G′(F_□)) and f^V_□ ∈ S(G^V(F_□)) have matching orbital integrals if O(δ^V, f^V_□) = Ω_□(γ)·O_η(γ, f′_□) for every matching pair γ ∈ G′_rs(F_□), δ^V ∈ G^V_rs(F_□). Here O(δ^V, ·) and O_η(γ, ·) are the relative orbital integrals defined as in (4.4) and (4.2) with A_F replaced by F_□, and Ω_□(γ) := ∏_{v∈□} Ω_v(γ) ∈ {±1} is the transfer factor of Beuzart-Plessis (arXiv:1602.06538, §§3.3–3.4), for which Ω_□(γ)O_η(γ, f′_□) depends only on the image of γ in B′(F_□). The same notion is used at a single place v (Propositions 4.6, 4.8) and for a family over the local hermitian pairs W with f^W = 0 for W ≠ V (the notation (g^V, 0, …)).
items.note: Split off from item 45. The transfer factor is a black box from [BP] = arXiv:1602.06538 (see E38 on the duplicated label [BP]). The invariance of Ω_□(γ)O_η(γ, f′) is asserted as 'clear' in the proof of Lemma 4.9, p. 36. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Definition 4.4(2): smooth transfer of (not necessarily pure tensor) Schwartz functions
items.statement: Let f′ ∈ S(G′(A_F)), not necessarily a pure tensor, V ∈ 𝔙 and f^V ∈ S(G^V(A_F)). Then f′ and f^V are smooth transfer if there is a sufficiently large finite set □ of places of F containing all archimedean places and all places ramified in E such that (a) f′ = f′_□ ⊗ ⊗_{v∉□} 1_{K′_v} with f′_□ ∈ S(G′(F_□)) and K′_v a relative hyperspecial maximal subgroup of G′(F_v); (b) f^V = f^V_□ ⊗ ⊗_{v∉□} 1_{K^V_v} with f^V_□ ∈ S(G^V(F_□)) and K^V_v a relative hyperspecial maximal subgroup of G^V(F_v); (c) f′_□ and f^V_□ have matching orbital integrals in the sense of Definition 4.4(1).
items.note: Split off from item 45. By Remark 4.5 (relative fundamental lemma, item 46) the notion does not depend on □. Condition (b) forces V_v to have a self-dual lattice for v ∉ □. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Definition 4.4(3): complete smooth transfer
items.statement: Let f′ ∈ S(G′(A_F)) and let (f^V)_{V∈𝔙} be a collection with f^V ∈ S(G^V(A_F)), all but finitely many of which are zero. Then f′ and (f^V)_{V∈𝔙} are complete smooth transfer if f′ and f^V are smooth transfer (Definition 4.4(2)) for every V ∈ 𝔙.
items.note: Split off from item 45. This is the hypothesis of Proposition 4.7. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: The setup S, K′, K^V, T and the base change maps bc^V_∞, bc^T_V, bc^V ((4.5)–(4.7))
items.statement: Let T_0 be the set of primes of F nonsplit in E. Fix a finite set S of primes of F containing those ramified in E, an open compact K′ = K′_S × ∏_{v∉S} K′_v ⊆ G′(A_F^∞) and, for V ∈ 𝔙, an open compact K^V = K^V_S × ∏_{v∉S} K^V_v ⊆ G^V(A_F^∞), with K′_v and K^V_v relative hyperspecial maximal subgroups (Definition 4.3) for every prime v ∉ S; put T = S ∪ T_0. The real groups G′ ⊗_Q R and G^V ⊗_Q R give root data, θ′ ⊆ Aut(X′*, Φ′, X′_*, Φ′^∨)^♡, θ^V, h′*, h^{V*}, W′, W^V as in §§2.2–2.3 (those for G^V do not depend on V, footnote 10). Base change on dual groups gives a canonical injective map h^{V*} → h′*, through which h^{V*} ⊆ h′*, and restriction defines the ring homomorphism bc^V_∞ : O(h′*_C)^{W′} → O(h^{V*}_C)^{W^V} (4.5). Unramified base change gives bc^T_V : H^T_{G′} → H^T_{G^V} (4.6), a convolution product, since all primes outside T split in E. Their tensor product is bc^V := bc^V_∞ ⊗ bc^T_V : O(h′*_C)^{W′} ⊗ H^T_{G′} → O(h^{V*}_C)^{W^V} ⊗ H^T_{G^V} (4.7). The proof of Proposition 4.8 uses, without stating it, the compatibility μ′(χ_{BC(π)}) = bc^V(μ′)(χ_π) for representations π of G^V unramified outside T.
items.note: Split off from item 51. Lemma 4.12 (p. 37) adds that bc^V_∞, bc^T_V and bc^V are surjective and that bc^V_∞ maps M(h′*_C)^{W′} into M(h^{V*}_C)^{W^V}. The setup is reused in §4.3 ('as in the previous subsection'). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Remark 4.10: Lemma 4.9 without the splitting assumption
items.statement: Lemma 4.9 holds, by the same proof, without assuming that the primes in □ are split in E. In that case the argument (more precisely, Beuzart-Plessis, Invent. Math. 2021, Theorem 5.4.1) relies on the endoscopic classification of Mok (Mem. AMS 2015) and Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White.
items.note: Split off from item 50. Used only in Remark 4.15 (p. 40). At inert primes, observation (2) in the proof of Lemma 4.9 also needs the p-adic local Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture, which [BP20] (archimedean) does not cover and the paper does not cite. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: 𝔙_(S) and the setup of §4.3
items.statement: Let S be a finite set of primes of F containing those ramified in E and T = S ∪ T_0. 𝔙_(S) is the set of V = (V_n, V_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔙 such that G^V_v is unramified for every prime v of F not in S. It is finite, and V_v = W_v in 𝔙_v for all V, W ∈ 𝔙_(S) and every prime v ∉ S. (For V ∈ 𝔙_(S) and v ∉ S, G^V(F_v) has relative hyperspecial subgroups K^V_v.) §4.3 fixes a nonempty subset 𝔙°_(S) ⊆ 𝔙_(S), a T-character χ′ of G′ (Definition 3.3) and, for each V ∈ 𝔙°_(S), a T-character χ^V of G^V whose base change is χ′, together with open compact K^V ⊆ G^V(A_F^∞) as in §4.2.
items.note: Used in Lemma 4.12, Proposition 4.13 and the proof of Theorem 1.8. Finiteness and the equality V_v = W_v are asserted without proof: finitely many local choices at S ∪ {∞} and the Hasse principle for hermitian spaces. At inert v ∉ S the pair is pinned down, because V_n and V_{n+1} = V_n ⊕ Ee have the same discriminant, one of them has even rank, and at inert v an even-rank unitary group is unramified only for the unit-discriminant form. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Positive-type local test functions (W. Zhang)
items.statement: (W. Zhang, Ann. of Math. 180 (2014), definition of positive type preceding Proposition 2.12; as used) Let V ∈ 𝔙 and π^V ∈ ℭ(G^V, 1), with 𝒫 nonzero on some cuspidal automorphic form in L²(G^V, π^V), and let S be a finite set of primes outside which E, V and π^V are unramified. For every place v that is archimedean or in S there is f_v ∈ S(G^V(F_v)) of positive type with J_{π^V_v}(f_v) > 0; at a prime v_0 split in E with π^V_{v_0} supercuspidal, f_{v_0} may be taken to be a supercuspidal matrix coefficient. For f^V = ⊗_{v ∈ S∪∞} f_v ⊗ ⊗_{v∉S} 1_{K^V_v} (K^V_v relative hyperspecial) one has J_{π^V}(f^V) > 0 and J_π(f^V) ⩾ 0 for every π ∈ ℭ(G^V, 1).
items.note: Split from item /54. The paper cites only the definition of positive type in [Zha14a]; the positivity statements are asserted ('By our choice of f^V'). They also use the nonvanishing of the local H^V-invariant functional on the K^V_v-spherical vector at v ∉ S (unramified computation). The precise formulation in [Zha14a] was not checked. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Asai L-functions of distinguished and hermitian cuspidal representations
items.statement: Let Π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_m(A_E). If L(s, Π, As^{(−1)^{m+1}}) has a pole at s = 1 (equivalently, by Flicker, Π is η_{E/F}^{m+1}-distinguished by GL_m(A_F)), then Π is conjugate self-dual and L(s, Π, As^{(−1)^m}) is regular at s = 1, so Π is hermitian (Definition 1.5). Conversely, if Π is hermitian then L(s, Π, As^{(−1)^{m+1}}) has a pole at s = 1.
items.locator: §4.3, proof of Proposition 4.13(2), p. 39; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.8, p. 41
items.note: Used without proof or reference: 'which implies that Π_m is hermitian' (p. 39) and 'since Π_m is hermitian, L(s, Π_m, As^{(−1)^{m+1}}) has a pole at s = 1' (p. 41). It follows from L(s, Π × Π^c) = L(s, Π, As^+)·L(s, Π, As^−), which has a simple pole at s = 1 exactly when Π^c ≅ Π^∨, and from distinction implying conjugate self-duality. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Heredity of genericity under parabolic induction (Rodier)
items.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean place, P = MN a parabolic subgroup of GL_N(F_v) and σ an irreducible admissible representation of M(F_v). The space of Whittaker functionals on I_P^{GL_N}(σ) has the same dimension as that of σ. Since the Whittaker functor is exact, if some irreducible subquotient of I_P^{GL_N}(σ) is generic then σ is generic.
items.note: Implicit (no reference in the paper). Used to deduce that σ°_v (resp. σ•_v) is generic at infinitely many split primes from π_v being generic and a constituent of I_{P}(σ_v) there. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Local components of isobaric sums of unitary cuspidal representations are generic
items.statement: If Π = Π_1 ⊞ ⋯ ⊞ Π_d with Π_i cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_{n_i}(A_E) with unitary central characters, then for every place w of E, Π_w = I_P(Π_{1,w} ⊗ ⋯ ⊗ Π_{d,w}) is irreducible and generic. In particular this holds for hermitian Π, whose constituents are conjugate self-dual and hence have unitary central characters.
items.note: Implicit. Local components of cuspidal representations are generic (Shalika), and induction from unitary generic representations of GL is irreducible (Bernstein, nonarchimedean; Vogan, archimedean). Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: Pure inner forms of unitary groups
items.statement: For a hermitian space V° over E of rank N, the pure inner forms of G° = U(V°) are the groups G• = U(V•) for hermitian spaces V• over E of rank N. In particular the G^V, V ∈ 𝔙, are the pure inner forms of the quasi-split G^{V*}.
items.locator: §4.3, Theorem 4.14(3) and proof, pp. 39–40; §4.4, proof of Theorem 1.8, p. 42
items.note: Used in the statement of Theorem 4.14(3); the proof unpacks it as 'a hermitian space V• of rank n+1 such that G• = U(V•)'. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: The unique quasi-split pair V* ∈ 𝔙
items.statement: There is a unique V* = (V*_n, V*_{n+1}) ∈ 𝔙 such that G^{V*} = U(V*_n) × U(V*_{n+1}) is quasi-split. V* lies in 𝔙_(S) for every finite set S of primes containing those ramified in E.
items.locator: §4.4, proofs of Theorem 1.8 ((1) ⇒ (2)) and Theorem 1.9, p. 42
items.note: Asserted without proof or reference (standard; Gan–Gross–Prasad). Locally the relevant pair is unique; globally it exists by the Hasse principle for hermitian spaces. Missing: routed to route 3.

items.name: Beuzart-Plessis's deduction of the Ichino–Ikeda formula from a global identity
items.statement: (Beuzart-Plessis, Invent. Math. 2021, proof of Theorem 5; as used) Let π = π_n ⊠ π_{n+1} be an everywhere tempered cuspidal automorphic representation of G^V with hermitian cuspidal weak base change Π. If there are factorizable f′ = ⊗_v f′_v ∈ S(G′(A_F))_{K′} and f^V = ⊗_v f^V_v ∈ S(G^V(A_F))_{K^V} such that f′_v and f^V_v have matching orbital integrals at every place v and I_Π(f′) = J_π(f^V) ≠ 0, then the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture (Harris's Conjecture 1.2) holds for π_n and π_{n+1}.
items.note: The paper says only 'The remaining argument is the same as in the proof of [BP21, Theorem 5]'. The global identity itself is obtained 'using the endoscopic classification for generic packets [Mok15, KMSW] and the local Gan–Gross–Prasad [BP20]' (items /62 and /9). Formulation as used; not checked against [BP21]. Missing: routed to route 2.

items.name: The reductions (A.2), (A.4) and (A.5) in the proof of Proposition A.1
items.statement: Let G = G(R) with G connected reductive over R, K a maximal compact subgroup, H^0 the identity component of a real Lie group H, Z = Z(R) and G_der = G_der(R). (A.2) K/K^0 → G/G^0 is a bijection, so C_c^∞(G)_{(K)} = ⊕_{k∈K/K^0} C_c^∞(kG^0)_{(K^0)}. Put K^0_Z = K ∩ Z^0, K^0_der = K ∩ G^0_der and Z^0_der = Z^0 ∩ G^0_der = K^0_Z ∩ K^0_der, a finite group (printed Z^0 ∩ G_der, see E47). Then (K^0_Z × K^0_der)/Z^0_der ≅ K^0 and (A.4) (Z^0 × G^0_der)/Z^0_der ≅ G^0. For finite sets 𝔗_Z, 𝔗_der of K^0_Z- and K^0_der-types, let 𝔗 be the set of K^0-types whose inflation to K^0_Z × K^0_der is an exterior tensor product of members of 𝔗_Z and 𝔗_der. For compact Ω_Z ⊆ Z^0 and Ω_der ⊆ G^0_der, bi-invariant under K^0_Z and K^0_der, let Ω ⊆ G^0 be the image of Ω_Z × Ω_der. Then C_c^∞(G^0)_{(K^0)} = ∪_Ω ∪_𝔗 C^∞_Ω(G^0)_{(𝔗)}, and (A.5) there is a natural isomorphism of Fréchet spaces (C^∞_{Ω_Z}(Z^0)_{(𝔗_Z)} ⊗̂ C^∞_{Ω_der}(G^0_der)_{(𝔗_der)})^{Z^0_der} ≅ C^∞_Ω(G^0)_{(𝔗)}.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.1, (A.2)–(A.5), pp. 43–44
items.note: Asserted without proof. Footnote 12: (A.5) fails in general without fixing the K^0-types and the support. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Paley–Wiener theorem for Schwartz functions on split real tori
items.statement: (classical) Let A be a split real analytic torus (A ≅ (R_{>0})^r) with cotangent space a*, and S(A) its space of Schwartz functions (smooth f with Df bounded for every algebraic differential operator D, i.e. f∘exp and all its derivatives decay faster than every exponential). The Fourier (Mellin) transform f ↦ (λ ↦ ∫_A f(a) a^λ da) is an isomorphism of Fréchet spaces from S(A) onto N(a*_C), the space of entire functions on a*_C with rapid decay on vertical strips.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Lemma A.2, p. 44
items.note: Split from item /41. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Schwartz functions on a product of Nash manifolds (Aizenbud–Gourevitch)
items.statement: (Aizenbud–Gourevitch, Israel J. Math. 177 (2010), Corollary 2.6.3) For Nash manifolds M and N, the natural map S(M) ⊗̂ S(N) → S(M × N) is an isomorphism of Fréchet spaces (S the Schwartz space of a Nash manifold, ⊗̂ the completed projective tensor product). Used for H^0 = Z^0_sp × H^0_der (Lemma A.2) and for the density of ⊗_{v|∞} S(G(F_v)) in S(G_∞) (proofs of Proposition 4.7 and Lemma 4.9).
items.locator: §4.2, proofs of Proposition 4.7 and Lemma 4.9, pp. 34–35; Appendix A, proof of Lemma A.2, p. 44
items.note: Split from item /41. For split tori, the Nash-manifold Schwartz space (R_{>0} as an open semialgebraic subset of R) agrees with the paper's Schwartz space S(A). Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Multipliers for the connected centre (Sakellaridis, Theorem 2.1.2)
items.statement: (Sakellaridis, arXiv:1804.02383, Theorem 2.1.2; as used) For μ_1 ∈ N(z*_C), a compact Ω_Z ⊆ Z^0 bi-invariant under K^0_Z and a finite set 𝔗_Z of K^0_Z-types, there is a linear map μ_1⋆ : C^∞_{Ω_Z}(Z^0)_{(𝔗_Z)} → S(Z^0)_{(𝔗_Z)} with ξ(μ_1⋆f) = μ_1(χ_ξ)·ξ(f) for every f and every smooth character ξ of Z^0 (χ_ξ ∈ z*_C its differential).
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.1, p. 44
items.note: Split from item /41. Not checked against [Sak]. For the abelian group Z^0 it also follows directly from the Paley–Wiener theorem. Missing: routed to route 1.

items.name: Separately continuous bilinear maps on Fréchet spaces (Trèves, Theorem 34.1)
items.statement: (Trèves, Topological vector spaces, distributions and kernels, 1967, Theorem 34.1) Let E and F be Fréchet spaces and G a locally convex space. Every separately continuous bilinear map E × F → G is continuous, and hence (universal property of the projective tensor product) extends uniquely to a continuous linear map E ⊗̂_π F → G when G is complete.
items.locator: Appendix A, proof of Proposition A.1, (A.6), p. 45
items.note: Split from item /41. The extension to ⊗̂ is the universal property of the completed projective tensor product; the paper cites both steps as [Trè67, Theorem 34.1]. Missing: routed to route 1.

routes.title: Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions, Part II: Schwartz multipliers and the isolation of cuspidal spectrum
routes.brief: Part II of Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions (AutomorphicSpectralTheory). It starts where that roadmap stops: AS.0–AS.4 build the functional analysis, Eisenstein series and the spectral decomposition of L² over cuspidal data, with compactly supported test functions; this Part II adds Schwartz test functions, their multipliers and the isolation of prescribed cuspidal components. Source: Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, 'Isolation of cuspidal spectrum, with application to the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture' (Ann. of Math. 194 (2021), 519–584; arXiv:1912.07169), §§2–3 and Appendix A. Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 2.13: for G connected reductive over R and every μ ∈ M_{θ∪{1}}(h*_C)^W there is a unique linear μ⋆ : S(G) → S(G) with π(μ⋆f) = μ(χ_π)π(f) for all irreducible admissible π (a continuous multiplier preserving bi-K-finite functions). Theorem 3.6: for a T-character χ that is not (G, T)-CAP there is a T-multiplier μ with μ(χ) = 1 such that R(μ⋆f) maps L²(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω) into L²_cusp(G(F)∖G(A_F)/K, ω)[χ] for all f ∈ S(G(A_F))_K. Theorem 3.7: for every χ, the same into L²_cusp[χ] from L²_cusp. Theorem 3.19: for every χ there is μ with μ(χ) = 1 whose R(μ⋆f) has image in the finite sum of cuspidal components L²_{(M,σ)} in which χ occurs. Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 (the nearly isotypic and Res_{F′/F}GL_n cases); Proposition A.1 (Delorme's multipliers on bi-K-finite C_c^∞ functions for reductive groups). Cover, in this order: (1) entire functions with prescribed zeros: Weierstrass products of finite rank and moderate vertical growth (Definitions 2.1, 2.3, Lemma 2.2, Proposition 2.4, Corollaries 2.5–2.6); (2) the spaces M_θ, N_θ, M^♯_θ attached to a root datum and the set θ of a real form, θ_G from maximal tori, and Lemmas 2.10, 2.19 (Definition 2.8, Remarks 2.9, 2.14–2.17); (3) the Schwartz algebra S(G) of a real reductive group (Wallach), with its L²-Sobolev description and relation to Harish-Chandra's L^p-Schwartz spaces; (4) Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula and the infinitesimal characters of tempered representations; Delorme's theorems (1984, 1986) and Proposition A.1 with Lemma A.2 (Paley–Wiener on split tori, Aizenbud–Gourevitch tensor products, Sakellaridis on the centre, Trèves); (5) difference operators on holomorphic functions (Lemmas 2.20, 2.21, 2.23, after Kostant–Kumar) and Kostant's tensor-product theorems with Lemma 2.22; (6) Proposition 2.24, Lemma 2.25 and Theorem 2.13, with minimal K-types and Lemma 2.18; (7) the adelic setup: Schwartz test functions, quasi-cuspidal functions, T-characters, CAP characters and T-multipliers (Definitions 3.1–3.5); (8) χ_∞-typical data, Donnelly's bound, Lemmas 3.12–3.14 and Proposition 3.15; (9) Definition 3.16, Proposition 3.17 (the Lindenstrauss–Venkatesh-style mixed multipliers), Theorem 3.19, Theorems 3.6–3.7, 1.1, 1.3 and Remark 3.20 (the refinement by Langlands components with Müller's trace class theorem). Import from: Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions (AutomorphicSpectralTheory) AS.0, AS.1 and AS.4, for the functional analysis, induced families and the decomposition of L² over cuspidal data; Automorphic forms on reductive groups (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups) AF.1–AF.3, for (g, K)-modules, the Harish-Chandra isomorphism and infinitesimal characters, Casselman–Wallach globalisation, automorphic forms, finiteness at fixed level and K-types, and cusp forms; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.4, for spherical Hecke algebras; Reductive algebraic groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups), for root data and real forms. Corrections the design must carry: Lemma 2.10 needs θ finite, which holds from §2.3 on but not for the set of all involutions of the root datum, which can be infinite (E16); the infinitesimal characters of irreducible (and of tempered) representations are contained in, not equal to, ⋃_ϑ h*_{ϑ,C} ⊕ Y*_ϑ, so the kernel description and the 'only if' half of the conjecture in Remark 2.16 fail (SU(2), SU(3)), while Theorem 2.13 uses only the inclusion (E19, E25); the proof of Lemma 2.18 must include limits of discrete series (E21); the roots of Kostant's polynomial in the proof of Lemma 2.22 are z(α + λ) under the usual action (E23); the proof of Lemma 3.12 must pass to finitely many conjugate levels (E34), and that of Lemma 3.13 must use the first χ_∞-typicality condition (E35); and in the proof of Proposition 3.17 for M = G the multiplier is μ⁰_∞ ⊗ h, not h (E36).
routes.reason: AutomorphicSpectralTheory owns the automorphic L²-spectrum and its decomposition over cuspidal data (AS.4), but only for compactly supported test functions; the Schwartz algebra, its multipliers and the isolation of cuspidal components extend that roadmap in its own direction and are used by every relative trace formula that needs cuspidal test functions (here Jacquet–Rallis; later papers in the queue by Beuzart-Plessis–Chaudouard–Zydor use the same device). Real harmonic analysis on S(G) (Harish-Chandra's Plancherel formula, Delorme's multipliers) is not planned anywhere and is only needed here, so it is planned in this Part II rather than in AF.1, which stops at (g, K)-modules and their globalisation.

routes.title: Endoscopic transfer and unitary trace comparison, Part II: Jacquet–Rallis relative transfer and Weil-equivariant trace comparison
routes.brief: This route coalesces with JacquetRallisRelativeTraceComparison, proposed by PAPER-ZHANG-21 (W. Zhang, Weil representation and arithmetic fundamental lemma); keep its id, title, parent, area and brief. That brief plans the Jacquet–Rallis relative quotients, matching, orbital integrals with transfer factors, local smooth and partial transfer, the partially linearised relative trace formula and the group and semi-Lie fundamental lemma. Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu, 'Isolation of cuspidal spectrum, with application to the Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture' (Ann. of Math. 194 (2021), 519–584; arXiv:1912.07169), §4 and §1.2, adds a global spectral layer on top of it. Final theorems of that layer, as the paper states them. Theorem 1.8: for hermitian cuspidal Π_n, Π_{n+1} of GL_n(A_E), GL_{n+1}(A_E), L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0 iff there are hermitian spaces V_n ⊂ V_{n+1} = V_n ⊕ Ee (e of norm 1), cuspidal π_m ⊆ A_cusp(U(V_m)) with BC(π_m) ≅ Π_m and cusp forms φ_m with ∫_{U(V_n)(F)∖U(V_n)(A_F)} φ_nφ_{n+1} ≠ 0 (Tamagawa measure). Theorem 1.9: every hermitian cuspidal Π_{n+1} admits a hermitian cuspidal Π_n with L(½, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0. Theorem 1.10: the Ichino–Ikeda conjecture for everywhere tempered pairs as in Theorem 1.8(2). Theorem 4.14: weak automorphic base change for unitary groups ((1) exists when π_v is generic at infinitely many split primes; (2) exists, cuspidal and hermitian, when π is supercuspidal at a split prime; (3) a hermitian base change forces π not CAP for any pure inner form; (4) then the archimedean infinitesimal characters match), proved without the endoscopic classification. Also Proposition 4.13 and Lemma 4.16. Add, after the candidate's local layers: (1) the global relative characters I_Π, J_π (Beuzart-Plessis) and Zydor's coarse relative trace formulas for quasi-cuspidal Schwartz test functions (Propositions 4.1–4.2); (2) smooth transfer in the global sense of Definition 4.4 with relative hyperspecial subgroups, existence of transfer on dense subspaces (W. Zhang, Xue; Proposition 4.6) and the relative fundamental lemma in all residue characteristics (Yun; Beuzart-Plessis), sharing the candidate's matching and transfer factors; (3) Chaudouard–Zydor's singular transfer (Proposition 4.7); (4) Beuzart-Plessis's local Plancherel formulas and comparison of relative characters, Lemma 4.9 and Remark 4.10; (5) base change of multipliers and Proposition 4.8, Proposition 4.11 (Gaussian test functions, consistent with the candidate's corrected Gaussians), Lemma 4.12; (6) positive-type test functions, the Burger–Sarnak trick, Flicker's Asai criterion and strong multiplicity one; (7) Proposition 4.13 and Theorem 4.14; (8) Lemma 4.16 with the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent, and the proofs of Theorems 1.8–1.10 (Remark 4.17). Treat as a proof obligation the archimedean compatibility in Proposition 4.13(1) when the weak base change is not cuspidal (sourceIssues E1): run the argument with the isolating multiplier of Theorem 3.19 on the general linear side, whose image is zero if the character occurs in no cuspidal datum. State as cited theorems, with their exact hypotheses, the extensions of Zydor's and Chaudouard–Zydor's results from C_c^∞ to Schwartz test functions, which the paper asserts without proof. Additional imports: The Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures for classical groups (GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups, proposed by PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20 and extended by this extraction) for hermitian representations, weak base change, the global and refined (Ichino–Ikeda) conjectures and the local Gan–Gross–Prasad theorems; Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions, Part II: Schwartz multipliers and the isolation of cuspidal spectrum (AutomorphicSpectralTheoryPartIISchwartzMultipliers, proposed here) for multipliers and isolation; Automorphic L-functions and local factors (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors) AL.3 for Rankin–Selberg integrals; Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) ML.4 for Mok's and Kaletha–Minguez–Shin–White's classification and ML.5 for the Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry descent; Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.2–SR.4. Corrections the design must carry: Proposition 4.7 is applied to transfers whose archimedean components lie in the completed Schwartz space, which Chaudouard–Zydor do not cover and density alone does not give; the design must supply that extension or keep the test functions in the algebraic tensor product (E39), and Theorems 1.8–1.10 and 4.14 rest on it; the proof of Proposition 4.13(1) covers only a cuspidal BC(π^V) and is completed by Theorem 3.19 (E1), and it must enlarge S so that π^V is unramified outside S (E43); Theorem 4.14(4) needs π cuspidal automorphic (E45); and the proof of Lemma 4.9 uses the twisted orbital integral O_η (E40).

routes.title: The Gan–Gross–Prasad conjectures for classical groups: relevant pairs, Vogan packets, Bessel models and periods
routes.brief: This route coalesces with GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups, proposed by PAPER-JIANG-ZHANG-20; keep its id, title, area and brief. Beuzart-Plessis–Liu–Zhang–Zhu (Ann. of Math. 194 (2021)) is one of the consumers that brief anticipates. It adds to the candidate's targets, for U(n) × U(n+1) (Bessel periods with ℓ = 0): hermitian isobaric representations of GL_n(A_E) (Definition 1.5: isobaric sums of distinct conjugate self-dual cuspidals with L(s, Π_i, As^{(−1)^n}) regular at s = 1); weak automorphic base change through the split places (Definition 1.6) and its uniqueness; the refined (Ichino–Ikeda) conjecture in R. N. Harris's formulation (IMRN 2014, Conjecture 1.2), which the brief reserves for the first consumer that needs it; and the local Gan–Gross–Prasad theorem for tempered unitary pairs (Beuzart-Plessis, Astérisque 418), with the injectivity of the local Jacquet–Langlands map on relevant tempered representations. That case only arises when F has at least two archimedean places, the typical case (F totally real, E CM). The same framework is used in later work (BPCZ, arXiv:2007.05601, §10.1, which takes transfers in the sense of BLZZ Definition 4.4 and cites [CZ] for them). A different write-up might avoid the issue by choosing archimedean multipliers as products over the archimedean places. For these reasons this is a gap in the proof, not an error in a stated result.
